author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)
description:
Detects the use of software that is related to the University of California, Berkeley via metadata information.
This indicates it may be related to BOINC software and can be used maliciously if unauthorized.
falsepositives: This software can be used for legitimate purposes when installed intentionally.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND Description='University of California, Berkeley')
title: Potential BOINC Software Execution (UC-Berkeley Signature)

author: frack113
description: Detects a user log-off activity. Could be used for example to correlate information during forensic investigations
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4634 OR EventID=4647)
title: User Logoff Event

author: frack113
description: Detects Windows update errors including installation failures and connection issues. Defenders should observe this in case critical update KBs aren't installed.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND (Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-WindowsUpdateClient' AND (EventID=16 OR EventID=20 OR EventID=24 OR EventID=213 OR EventID=217))
title: Windows Update Error

author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)
description: A General detection for specific decompress commands in PowerShell logs. This could be an adversary decompressing files.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND Payload LIKE '%Expand-Archive%' ESCAPE '\')
title: PowerShell Decompress Commands

author: Cian Heasley
description: Windows Defender logs when the history of detected infections is deleted.
falsepositives: Deletion of Defender malware detections history for legitimate reasons
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' AND EventID=1013
title: Windows Defender Malware Detection History Deletion

author: frack113
description: ForceV1 asks for information directly from the kernel space. Conhost connects to the console application. High IntegrityLevel means the process is running with elevated privileges, such as an Administrator context.
falsepositives: Very Likely, including launching cmd.exe via Run As Administrator
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((IntegrityLevel='High' OR IntegrityLevel='S-1-16-12288') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%conhost.exe%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%0xffffffff%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-ForceV1%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious High IntegrityLevel Conhost Legacy Option

author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime
description: Detects locked workstation session events that occur automatically after a standard period of inactivity.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4800
title: Locked Workstation

author: Thomas Patzke
description: Detects code integrity failures such as missing page hashes or corrupted drivers due unauthorized modification. This could be a sign of tampered binaries.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5038 OR EventID=6281) AND (NOT COALESCE(((param1 LIKE '%\\CSFalconServiceUninstallTool\_%' ESCAPE '\' OR param1 LIKE '%\\Program Files\\CrowdStrike\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR param1 LIKE '%\\System32\\drivers\\CrowdStrike\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR param1 LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\ScriptControl64\_%' ESCAPE '\') OR param1 LIKE '%\\Program Files\\Sophos\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Failed Code Integrity Checks

author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)
description: A General detection for a new application in AppCompat. This indicates an application executing for the first time on an endpoint.
falsepositives: This rule is to explore new applications on an endpoint. False positives depends on the organization.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\AppCompatFlags\\Compatibility Assistant\\Store\\%' ESCAPE '\')
title: New Application in AppCompat

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may attempt to get information about running processes on a system. Information obtained could be used to gain an understanding of common software/applications running on systems within the network
falsepositives: Likely from users, administrator and different internal and third party applications.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%tasklist%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\tasklist.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='tasklist.exe'))
title: Suspicious Tasklist Discovery Command

author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR)
description: Detects the registration of the security event source VSSAudit. It would usually trigger when volume shadow copy operations happen.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of VSSVC. Maybe backup operations. It would usually be done by C:\Windows\System32\VSSVC.exe.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (AuditSourceName='VSSAudit' AND (EventID=4904 OR EventID=4905))
title: VSSAudit Security Event Source Registration

author: lazarg
description: Detects attempts to query system information directly from the Windows Registry.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%query%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-v%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/v%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%–v%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%—v%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%―v%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Get-ItemPropertyValue%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%gpv%' ESCAPE '\'))) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Uninstall%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\TimeZoneInformation%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: System Information Discovery via Registry Queries

author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects activity when the settings of the Windows firewall have been changed
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security/Firewall' AND (EventID=2002 OR EventID=2083 OR EventID=2003 OR EventID=2082 OR EventID=2008)
title: Windows Firewall Settings Have Been Changed

author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime
description: Detects activity when a member is removed from a security-enabled global group
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=633 OR EventID=4729)
title: A Member Was Removed From a Security-Enabled Global Group

author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of findstr with the "s" and "i" flags for a "subfolder" and "insensitive" search respectively. Attackers sometimes leverage this built-in utility to search the system for interesting files or filter through results of commands.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%findstr%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%findstr.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='FINDSTR.EXE') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '% -s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―s %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -i %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /i %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –i %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —i %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―i %' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Insensitive Subfolder Search Via Findstr.EXE

author: frack113
description: Detects activity when Windows Defender Firewall has been reset to its default configuration
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security/Firewall' AND (EventID=2032 OR EventID=2060)
title: Windows Defender Firewall Has Been Reset To Its Default Configuration

author: Ali Alwashali
description: Detects command execution via ScreenConnect RMM
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name='ScreenConnect' AND EventID=200 AND Data LIKE '%Executed command of length%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Command Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects DNS queries to "ufile.io", which was seen abused by malware and threat actors as a method for data exfiltration
falsepositives: DNS queries for "ufile" are not malicious by nature necessarily. Investigate the source to determine the necessary actions to take
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-DNS Client Events/Operational' AND (EventID=3008 AND QueryName LIKE '%ufile.io%' ESCAPE '\')
title: DNS Query To Ufile.io - DNS Client

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects access to ADMIN$ network share
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5140 AND ShareName='Admin$') AND (NOT COALESCE((SubjectUserName LIKE '%$' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Access To ADMIN$ Network Share

author: frack113, Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io'
description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\netsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='netsh.exe') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%netsh%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%show %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%firewall %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%config %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%state %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%rule %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%name=all%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Firewall Configuration Discovery Via Netsh.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects changes to the "MaxMpxCt" registry value.
MaxMpxCt specifies the maximum outstanding network requests for the server per client, which is used when negotiating a Server Message Block (SMB) connection with a client. Note if the value is set beyond 125 older Windows 9x clients will fail to negotiate.
Ransomware threat actors and operators (specifically BlackCat) were seen increasing this value in order to handle a higher volume of traffic.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Services\\LanmanServer\\Parameters\\MaxMpxCt' ESCAPE '\')
title: MaxMpxCt Registry Value Changed

author: frack113
description: Detects usage of the "systeminfo" command to retrieve information
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\systeminfo.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='sysinfo.exe'))
title: Suspicious Execution of Systeminfo

author: juju4
description: Detect remote login by Administrator user (depending on internal pattern).
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND LogonType=10 AND AuthenticationPackageName='Negotiate' AND TargetUserName LIKE 'Admin%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Admin User Remote Logon

author: Center for Threat Informed Defense (CTID) Summiting the Pyramid Team
description:
Detects "read access" requests on the services registry key.
Adversaries may execute their own malicious payloads by hijacking the Registry entries used by services.
Adversaries may use flaws in the permissions for Registry keys related to services to redirect from the originally specified executable to one that they control, in order to launch their own code when a service starts.
falsepositives: Likely from legitimate applications reading their key. Requires heavy tuning
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4663 AND (ObjectName LIKE '%\\SYSTEM\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ObjectName LIKE '%ControlSet\\Services\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND AccessList LIKE '%\%\%1538%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Service Registry Key Read Access Request

author: frack113
description:
Detects the execution of "wmic" with the "group" flag.
Adversaries may attempt to find local system groups and permission settings.
The knowledge of local system permission groups can help adversaries determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group.
Adversaries may use this information to determine which users have elevated permissions, such as the users found within the local administrators group.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wmic.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='wmic.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '% group%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Local Groups Reconnaissance Via Wmic.EXE

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
description:
Detects registry modifications related to the proxy configuration of the system, potentially associated with the Raspberry Robin malware, as seen in campaigns running in Q1 2024.
Raspberry Robin may alter proxy settings to circumvent security measures, ensuring unhindered connection with Command and Control servers for maintaining control over compromised systems if there are any proxy settings that are blocking connections.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Downloads\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\control.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Internet Settings\\ZoneMap\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (((TargetObject LIKE '%\\IntranetName' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\ProxyByPass' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\UNCAsIntranet' ESCAPE '\') AND NewValue LIKE '%DWORD (0x00000001)%' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\AutoDetect' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '%DWORD (0x00000000)%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Potential Raspberry Robin Registry Set Internet Settings ZoneMap

author: Michael Haag, Mark Woan (improvements), James Pemberton / @4A616D6573 / oscd.community (improvements)
description: Detects execution of "Net.EXE".
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '% accounts%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% group%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% localgroup%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% share%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% start%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% stop %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% user%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% view%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Net.EXE Execution

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries with no prior knowledge of legitimate credentials within the system or environment may guess passwords to attempt access to accounts.
Without knowledge of the password for an account, an adversary may opt to systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapDirectoryIdentifier%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%System.Net.NetworkCredential%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious Connection to Remote Account

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may employ a known encryption algorithm to conceal command and control traffic rather than relying on any inherent protections provided by a communication protocol.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%System.Net.Security.SslStream%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Net.Security.RemoteCertificateValidationCallback%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%.AuthenticateAsClient%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious SSL Connection

author: Avneet Singh @v3t0_, oscd.community, Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock (updated)
description: This rule detects the execution of Run Once task as configured in the registry
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\runonce.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Description='Run Once Wrapper') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/AlternateShellStartup%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/r' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Run Once Task Execution as Configured in Registry

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects plugged/unplugged USB devices
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-DriverFrameworks-UserMode/Operational' AND (EventID=2003 OR EventID=2100 OR EventID=2102)
title: USB Device Plugged

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system they are currently accessing or from remote systems by querying for information over the network.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe')) AND ((CommandLine LIKE '% use' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% sessions' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '% use %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% sessions %' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: System Network Connections Discovery Via Net.EXE

author: frack113
description: Detects the creation of a new bits job by Bitsadmin
falsepositives: Many legitimate applications or scripts could leverage "bitsadmin". This event is best correlated with EID 16403 via the JobID field
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND processPath LIKE '%\\bitsadmin.exe' ESCAPE '\')
title: New BITS Job Created Via Bitsadmin

author: frack113
description: Detects the creation or removal of a computer. Can be used to detect attacks such as DCShadow via the creation of a new SPN.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4741 OR EventID=4743)
title: Add or Remove Computer from DC

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), j4son
description: Detects failed logon attempts from clients to MSSQL server.
falsepositives: This event could stem from users changing an account's password that's used to authenticate via a job or an automated process. Investigate the source of such events and mitigate them
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name LIKE '%MSSQL%' ESCAPE '\' AND EventID=18456)
title: MSSQL Server Failed Logon

author: Markus Neis
description: Detects the execution of a Sysinternals Tool via the creation of the "accepteula" registry key
falsepositives: Programs that use the same Registry Key
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\EulaAccepted' ESCAPE '\')
title: PUA - Sysinternal Tool Execution - Registry

author: frack113
description:
This tool enables enumeration and exporting of all DNS records in the zone for recon purposes of internal networks Python 3 and python.exe must be installed,
Usee to Query/modify DNS records for Active Directory integrated DNS via LDAP
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\python.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%adidnsdump%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: PUA - Adidnsdump Execution

author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects successful MSIX/AppX package installations on Windows systems by monitoring EventID 854 in the Microsoft-Windows-AppXDeployment-Server/Operational log.
While most installations are legitimate, this can help identify unauthorized or suspicious package installations.
It is crucial to monitor such events as threat actors may exploit MSIX/AppX packages to deliver and execute malicious payloads.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-AppXDeploymentServer/Operational' AND EventID=854
title: Successful MSIX/AppX Package Installation

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may abuse container files such as disk image (.iso, .vhd) file formats to deliver malicious payloads that may not be tagged with MOTW.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Mount-DiskImage %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-ImagePath %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious Mount-DiskImage

author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community
description: Detects the usage of the "net.exe" command to start a service using the "start" flag
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user executes a service for legitimate reasons.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe')) AND CommandLine LIKE '% start %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Start Windows Service Via Net.EXE

author: Harish Segar, frack113
description: Detects a renamed Powershell execution, which is a common technique used to circumvent security controls and bypass detection logic that's dependent on process names and process paths.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Windows PowerShell' AND (EventID=400 AND (Data LIKE '%HostName=ConsoleHost%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE(((Data LIKE '%HostApplication=powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%HostApplication=C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%HostApplication=C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%HostApplication=C:/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%HostApplication=C:/Windows/SysWOW64/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%HostApplication=C:\\\\WINDOWS\\\\system32\\\\WindowsPowerShell\\\\v1.0\\\\powershell.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%HostApplication=C:\\\\WINDOWS\\\\SysWOW64\\\\WindowsPowerShell\\\\v1.0\\\\powershell.exe%' ESCAPE '\') OR Data REGEXP 'HostId=[a-zA-Z0-9-]{36}\s+EngineVersion='), 0))))
title: Renamed Powershell Under Powershell Channel

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects PowerShell download activity, via the .DownloadFile() or .DownloadString() methods of the Net.WebClient class.
This technique is often abused by attackers to download additional payloads.
falsepositives: This activity may be used by legitimate software, such as patch management tools or software updaters. Investigate any such activity and apply the necessary filter.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Windows PowerShell' AND (EventID=400 AND (Data LIKE '%Net.WebClient%' ESCAPE '\' AND (Data LIKE '%.DownloadFile(%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%.DownloadString(%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PowerShell Download Via Net.WebClient - PowerShell Classic

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the registration of a new ODBC driver.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\ODBC\\ODBCINST.INI\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Driver' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetObject LIKE '%\\SQL Server\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '\%WINDIR\%\\System32\\SQLSRV32.dll' ESCAPE '\'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft Access %' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE 'C:\\Progra%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '%\\ACEODBC.DLL' ESCAPE '\') OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft Excel Driver%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE 'C:\\Progra%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '%\\ACEODBC.DLL' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: New ODBC Driver Registered

author: frack113
description: Detects usage of the "Get-AdComputer" to enumerate Computers or properties within Active Directory.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-AdComputer %' ESCAPE '\' AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Filter %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-LDAPFilter %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Properties %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Active Directory Computers Enumeration With Get-AdComputer

author: frack113
description:
Detects execution of the builtin "del"/"erase" commands in order to delete files.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was done within a network and how.
Removal of these files can occur during an intrusion, or as part of a post-intrusion process to minimize the adversary's footprint.
falsepositives: False positives levels will differ Depending on the environment. You can use a combination of ParentImage and other keywords from the CommandLine field to filter legitimate activity
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%del %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%erase %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -f%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /f%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –f%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —f%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―f%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -q%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /q%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –q%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —q%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―q%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: File Deletion Via Del

author: The DFIR Report
description: Detects the execution of Notepad to open a file that has the string "password" which may indicate unauthorized access to credentials or suspicious activity.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of opening files from remote hosts by administrators or users. However, storing passwords in text readable format could potentially be a violation of the organization's policy. Any match should be investigated further.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\notepad.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%password%.txt' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%password%.csv' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%password%.doc' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%password%.xls' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Notepad Password Files Discovery

author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community
description:
Detects file association changes using the builtin "assoc" command.
When a file is opened, the default program used to open the file (also called the file association or handler) is checked. File association selections are stored in the Windows Registry and can be edited by users, administrators, or programs that have Registry access or by administrators using the built-in assoc utility. Applications can modify the file association for a given file extension to call an arbitrary program when a file with the given extension is opened.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '%assoc%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Change Default File Association Via Assoc

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the creation of a process via the Windows task manager. This might be an attempt to bypass UAC
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\taskmgr.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\mmc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\resmon.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\Taskmgr.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: New Process Created Via Taskmgr.EXE

author: frack113
description: Detects the use of PowerShell to identify the current logged user.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%[System.Environment]::UserName%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%$env:UserName%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%[System.Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious PowerShell Get Current User

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), AdmU3
description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to create a compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities to compress or encrypt data before exfiltration.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\tar.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='bsdtar') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-c%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-r%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-u%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Compressed File Creation Via Tar.EXE

author: frack113
description:
Detects execution of the builtin "rmdir" command in order to delete directories.
Adversaries may delete files left behind by the actions of their intrusion activity.
Malware, tools, or other non-native files dropped or created on a system by an adversary may leave traces to indicate to what was done within a network and how.
Removal of these files can occur during an intrusion, or as part of a post-intrusion process to minimize the adversary's footprint.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '%rmdir%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/q%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Directory Removal Via Rmdir

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of the "Import-Module" cmdlet in order to add new Cmdlets to the current PowerShell session
falsepositives: Depending on the environement, many legitimate scripts will import modules inline. This rule is targeted for hunting purposes.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Import-Module %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ipmo %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal\_%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\cmd.exe%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Visual Studio\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%Tools\\Microsoft.VisualStudio.DevShell.dll%' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Import New Module Via PowerShell CommandLine

author: Daniel Koifman (@Koifsec), Nasreddine Bencherchali
description: Detects file access requests to browser credential stores by uncommon processes. Could indicate potential attempt of credential stealing This rule requires heavy baselining before usage.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4663 AND ObjectType='File' AND AccessMask='0x1') AND ((ObjectName LIKE '%\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '%\\User Data\\Local State%' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '%\\User Data\\Default\\Network\\Cookies%' ESCAPE '\') OR (FileName LIKE '%\\cookies.sqlite' ESCAPE '\' OR FileName LIKE '%\\places.sqlite' ESCAPE '\' OR FileName LIKE '%release\\key3.db' ESCAPE '\' OR FileName LIKE '%release\\key4.db' ESCAPE '\' OR FileName LIKE '%release\\logins.json' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName='System' OR (ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\system32\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\')), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND (ProcessName LIKE '%\\MpCopyAccelerator.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: Access To Browser Credential Files By Uncommon Applications - Security

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to the "TracingDisabled" key in order to disable ETW logging for services.exe (SCM)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%Software\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Tracing\\SCM\\Regular\\TracingDisabled' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)'))
title: ETW Logging Disabled For SCM

author: frack113
description:
Detects the use of the redirection character ">" to redirect information on the command line.
This technique is sometimes used by malicious actors in order to redirect the output of reconnaissance commands such as "hostname" and "dir" to files for future exfiltration.
falsepositives: Internet Download Manager extensions use named pipes and redirection via CLI. Filter it out if you use it in your environment
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%>%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Internet Download Manager\\IDMMsgHost.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%chrome-extension://%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\.\\pipe\\chrome.nativeMessaging%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: CMD Shell Output Redirect

author: David Strassegger, Tim Shelton
description: Detects scheduled task deletion events. Scheduled tasks are likely to be deleted if not used for persistence. Malicious Software often creates tasks directly under the root node e.g. \TASKNAME
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4699 AND (NOT COALESCE((TaskName LIKE '\\Microsoft\\Windows\\RemovalTools\\MRT\_ERROR\_HB' ESCAPE '\' OR TaskName LIKE '%\\Mozilla\\Firefox Default Browser Agent %' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Scheduled Task Deletion

author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community
description: Local accounts, System Owner/User discovery using operating systems utilities
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user enumerates local users for legitimate reason
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '% /c%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%dir %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '% rmdir %' ESCAPE '\'), 0))) OR (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%user%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%/domain%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/add%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/delete%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/active%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/expires%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/passwordreq%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/scriptpath%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/times%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/workstations%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))) OR (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\whoami.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\quser.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\qwinsta.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='whoami.exe' OR OriginalFileName='quser.exe' OR OriginalFileName='qwinsta.exe')) OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wmic.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%useraccount%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%get%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmdkey.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% /l%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Local Accounts Discovery

author: frack113
description: Detects calls to the "New-NetFirewallRule" cmdlet from PowerShell in order to add a new firewall rule with an "Allow" action.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell\_ise.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%New-NetFirewallRule %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% -Action %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%allow%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: New Windows Firewall Rule Added Via New-NetFirewallRule Cmdlet

author: frack113
description:
Detects the execution of the "jsc.exe" (JScript Compiler).
Attacker might abuse this in order to compile JScript files on the fly and bypassing application whitelisting.
falsepositives: Legitimate use to compile JScript by developers.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\jsc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='jsc.exe'))
title: JScript Compiler Execution

author: Cybex
description:
Detects potential exploitation attempts of CVE-2022-21919 or CVE-2021-34484 leading to local privilege escalation via the User Profile Service.
During exploitation of this vulnerability, two logs (Provider_Name: Microsoft-Windows-User Profiles Service) with EventID 1511 and 1515 are created (EventID 1515 may generate many false positives).
Additionally, the directory \Users\TEMP may be created during exploitation. This behavior was observed on Windows Server 2008.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (EventID=1511 AND Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-User Profiles Service')
title: Potential Exploitation of CVE-2022-21919 or CVE-2021-34484 for LPE

author: Joseph Kamau
description:
Detects web browser process opening an HTML file from a user's Downloads folder.
This behavior is could be associated with phishing attacks where threat actors send HTML attachments to users.
When a user opens such an attachment, it can lead to the execution of malicious scripts or the download of malware.
During investigation, analyze the HTML file for embedded scripts or links, check for any subsequent downloads or process executions, and investigate the source of the email or message containing the attachment.
falsepositives: Opening any HTML file located in users directories via a browser process will trigger this.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\brave.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\chrome.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\firefox.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msedge.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\opera.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\vivaldi.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%:\\users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Downloads\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.htm%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: HTML File Opened From Download Folder

author: frack113
description: Detects when a rule has been modified in the Windows firewall exception list
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security/Firewall' AND ((EventID=2005 OR EventID=2073) AND (NOT COALESCE((ApplicationPath LIKE '%\\AppData\\local\\microsoft\\teams\\current\\teams.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ApplicationPath LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Keybase\\keybase.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ApplicationPath LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Messenger\\Messenger.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR (ApplicationPath LIKE '%:\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ApplicationPath LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Opera\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ApplicationPath LIKE '%\\opera.exe%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ApplicationPath LIKE '%:\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ApplicationPath LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\BraveSoftware\\Brave-Browser\\Application\\brave.exe%' ESCAPE '\')), 0)))
title: Firewall Rule Modified In The Windows Firewall Exception List

author: frack113
description: An application has been removed. Check if it is critical.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name='MsiInstaller' AND (EventID=1034 OR EventID=11724))
title: Application Uninstalled

author: frack113
description: Detects execution of "sc.exe" to query information about registered services on the system
falsepositives: Legitimate query of a service by an administrator to get more information such as the state or PID
Keybase process "kbfsdokan.exe" query the dokan1 service with the following commandline "sc query dokan1"
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sc.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND OriginalFileName='sc.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '% query%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine='sc query dokan1'), 0))))
title: SC.EXE Query Execution

author: Thomas Patzke
description: Detects successful logon attempts performed with WMI
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND ProcessName LIKE '%\\WmiPrvSE.exe' ESCAPE '\')
title: Successful Account Login Via WMI

author: Ali Alwashali
description: Detects file being transferred via ScreenConnect RMM
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name='ScreenConnect' AND EventID=201 AND Data LIKE '%Transferred files with action%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect File Transfer

author: Orlinum , BlueDefenZer
description: Detects certificate creation with template allowing risk permission subject
falsepositives: Proxy SSL certificate with subject modification
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4898 AND TemplateContent LIKE '%CT\_FLAG\_ENROLLEE\_SUPPLIES\_SUBJECT%' ESCAPE '\') OR (EventID=4899 AND NewTemplateContent LIKE '%CT\_FLAG\_ENROLLEE\_SUPPLIES\_SUBJECT%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: ADCS Certificate Template Configuration Vulnerability

author: Eli Salem, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community
description: Detects the execution of regini.exe which can be used to modify registry keys, the changes are imported from one or more text files.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regini.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='REGINI.EXE') AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine REGEXP ':[^ \\]'), 0))))
title: Registry Modification Via Regini.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Christopher Peacock @securepeacock
description: Detects potential RDP connection via Mstsc using a local ".rdp" file
falsepositives: Likely with legitimate usage of ".rdp" files
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\mstsc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='mstsc.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%.rdp' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.rdp"' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\lxss\\wslhost.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\WSL\\wslg.rdp%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Mstsc.EXE Execution With Local RDP File

author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g
description: Detects remote PowerShell sessions
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Windows PowerShell' AND (EventID=400 AND (Data LIKE '%HostName=ServerRemoteHost%' ESCAPE '\' AND Data LIKE '%wsmprovhost.exe%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Remote PowerShell Session (PS Classic)

author: Endgame, JHasenbusch (ported for oscd.community)
description: Detects attempts to enumerate file shares, printer shares and sessions using "net.exe" with the "view" flag.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of net.exe utility by legitimate user
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%view%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%\\\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Share And Session Enumeration Using Net.EXE

author: Agro (@agro_sev) oscd.community
description:
Windows Test Authoring and Execution Framework (TAEF) framework allows you to run automation by executing tests files written on different languages (C, C#, Microsoft COM Scripting interfaces
Adversaries may execute malicious code (such as WSC file with VBScript, dll and so on) directly by running te.exe
falsepositives: It's not an uncommon to use te.exe directly to execute legal TAEF tests
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\te.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\te.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName LIKE '\\te.exe' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Malicious Windows Script Components File Execution by TAEF Detection

author: Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io'
description: Attackers may leverage fsutil to enumerated connected drives.
falsepositives: Certain software or administrative tasks may trigger false positives.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\fsutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='fsutil.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '%drives%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Fsutil Drive Enumeration

author: frack113
description:
Detects the execution of "RegAsm.exe" without a commandline flag or file, which might indicate potential process injection activity.
Usually "RegAsm.exe" should point to a dedicated DLL file or call the help with the "/?" flag.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Regasm by developers.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\RegAsm.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='RegAsm.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%RegAsm' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%RegAsm.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%RegAsm.exe"' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%RegAsm.exe''' ESCAPE '\')))
title: RegAsm.EXE Execution Without CommandLine Flags or Files

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), MahirAli Khan (in/mahiralikhan)
description:
Detects the use of the "SET" internal command of Cmd.EXE with the /p flag followed directly by an "=" sign.
Attackers used this technique along with an append redirection operator ">>" in order to update the content of a file indirectly.
Ex: cmd /c >> example.txt set /p="test data". This will append "test data" to contents of "example.txt".
The typical use case of the "set /p=" command is to prompt the user for input.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the SET with the "/p" flag for user prompting. command in administrative scripts or user-generated scripts.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/c set /p=%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%"set /p=%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%>>%set /p=%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential File Override/Append Via SET Command

author: Patrick Bareiss
description: Detects local user creation on Windows servers, which shouldn't happen in an Active Directory environment. Apply this Sigma Use Case on your Windows server logs and not on your DC logs.
falsepositives: Local accounts managed by privileged account management tools
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4720
title: Local User Creation

author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Dan Beavin), oscd.community
description: Detects the execution of "hh.exe" to open ".chm" files.
falsepositives: False positives are expected with legitimate ".CHM"
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((OriginalFileName='HH.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\hh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%.chm%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: HH.EXE Execution

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may look for folders and drives shared on remote systems as a means of identifying sources of information to gather as a precursor for Collection and
to identify potential systems of interest for Lateral Movement.
Networks often contain shared network drives and folders that enable users to access file directories on various systems across a network.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND (Payload LIKE '%get-smbshare%' ESCAPE '\' OR ContextInfo LIKE '%get-smbshare%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious Get Information for SMB Share - PowerShell Module

author: @neu5ron, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects scenarios where system auditing (i.e.: Windows event log auditing) is disabled.
This may be used in a scenario where an entity would want to bypass local logging to evade detection when Windows event logging is enabled and reviewed.
Also, it is recommended to turn off "Local Group Policy Object Processing" via GPO, which will make sure that Active Directory GPOs take precedence over local/edited computer policies via something such as "gpedit.msc".
Please note, that disabling "Local Group Policy Object Processing" may cause an issue in scenarios of one off specific GPO modifications - however, it is recommended to perform these modifications in Active Directory anyways.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4719 AND (AuditPolicyChanges LIKE '%\%\%8448%' ESCAPE '\' OR AuditPolicyChanges LIKE '%\%\%8450%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9210-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9211-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9212-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9215-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9217-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE921B-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE922B-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE922F-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9230-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9235-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9236-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9237-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE923F-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9240-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}' OR SubcategoryGuid='{0CCE9242-69AE-11D9-BED3-505054503030}'), 0)))
title: Windows Event Auditing Disabled

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to the AppInstaller (winget) admin settings. Such as enabling local manifest installations or disabling installer hash checks
falsepositives: The event doesn't contain information about the type of change. False positives are expected with legitimate changes
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\winget.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '\\REGISTRY\\A\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\LocalState\\admin\_settings' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Winget Admin Settings Modification

author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community
description:
Detects PowerShell scripts that make use of the "Compress-Archive" cmdlet in order to compress folders and files.
An adversary might compress data (e.g., sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Compress-Archive%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Compress-Archive Cmdlet Execution

author: Timur Zinniatullin, E.M. Anhaus, oscd.community
description: Detects usage of "rar" to add files to an archive for potential compression. An adversary may compress data (e.g. sensitive documents) that is collected prior to exfiltration in order to make it portable and minimize the amount of data sent over the network.
falsepositives: Highly likely if rar is a default archiver in the monitored environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\rar.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% a %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Files Added To An Archive Using Rar.EXE

author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Adversaries may enumerate browser bookmarks to learn more about compromised hosts.
Browser bookmarks may reveal personal information about users (ex: banking sites, interests, social media, etc.) as well as details about
internal network resources such as servers, tools/dashboards, or other related infrastructure.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\where.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='where.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%places.sqlite%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cookies.sqlite%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%formhistory.sqlite%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%logins.json%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%key4.db%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%key3.db%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%sessionstore.jsonlz4%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%History%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Bookmarks%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Cookies%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Login Data%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Where Execution

author: frack113
description: Use of hostname to get information
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\HOSTNAME.EXE' ESCAPE '\')
title: Suspicious Execution of Hostname

author: frack113
description: Detects usage of the "dir" command part of Windows CMD with the "/S" command line flag in order to enumerate files in a specified directory and all subdirectories.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%-s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%–s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%—s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%―s%' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%dir %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%rmdir%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: File And SubFolder Enumeration Via Dir Command

author: Markus Neis
description: Detects command lines that contain the 'accepteula' flag which could be a sign of execution of one of the Sysinternals tools
falsepositives: Programs that use the same command line flag
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -accepteula%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /accepteula%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –accepteula%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —accepteula%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―accepteula%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potential Execution of Sysinternals Tools

author: frack113
description: Detects activity when The Windows Defender Firewall service failed to load Group Policy
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security/Firewall' AND EventID=2009
title: The Windows Defender Firewall Service Failed To Load Group Policy

author: Josh Nickels, mttaggart
description:
Detects the execution of "BitLockerToGo.EXE".
BitLocker To Go is BitLocker Drive Encryption on removable data drives. This feature includes the encryption of, USB flash drives, SD cards, External hard disk drives, Other drives that are formatted by using the NTFS, FAT16, FAT32, or exFAT file system.
This is a rarely used application and usage of it at all is worth investigating.
Malware such as Lumma stealer has been seen using this process as a target for process hollowing.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of BitLockerToGo.exe to encrypt portable devices.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\BitLockerToGo.exe' ESCAPE '\')
title: BitLockerTogo.EXE Execution

author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov, Harish Segar
description:
Detects powershell execution with that make use of to the bxor (Bitwise XOR).
Attackers might use as an alternative obfuscation method to Base64 encoded commands.
Investigate the CommandLine and process tree to determine if the activity is malicious.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Windows PowerShell' AND (EventID=400 AND (Data LIKE '%HostName=ConsoleHost%' ESCAPE '\' AND Data LIKE '% -bxor %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: bXOR Operator Usage In PowerShell Command Line - PowerShell Classic

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may attempt to find domain-level groups and permission settings.
The knowledge of domain-level permission groups can help adversaries determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group.
Adversaries may use this information to determine which users have elevated permissions, such as domain administrators.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND ((Payload LIKE '%get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership%' ESCAPE '\' OR ContextInfo LIKE '%get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership%' ESCAPE '\') OR ((Payload LIKE '%get-aduser%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%-f %' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%-pr %' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%DoesNotRequirePreAuth%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ContextInfo LIKE '%get-aduser%' ESCAPE '\' AND ContextInfo LIKE '%-f %' ESCAPE '\' AND ContextInfo LIKE '%-pr %' ESCAPE '\' AND ContextInfo LIKE '%DoesNotRequirePreAuth%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: AD Groups Or Users Enumeration Using PowerShell - PoshModule

author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the "sc.exe" utility
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behavior in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((OriginalFileName='sc.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sc.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '% stop %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Stop Windows Service Via Sc.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Thurein Oo
description: Detects the enabling of the PowerShell script execution policy. Once enabled, this policy allows scripts to be executed.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\PowerShell\\EnableScripts' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)'))
title: PowerShell Script Execution Policy Enabled

author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community
description: Detects the creation of a new service using the "sc.exe" utility.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user creates a service for legitimate reasons.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sc.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%create%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%binPath%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Dropbox\\Client\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Dropbox\\Client\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\Dropbox.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: New Service Creation Using Sc.EXE

author: frack113, MalGamy (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali
description:
Detects execution of "taskkill.exe" in order to stop a service or a process. Look for suspicious parents executing this command in order to hunt for potential malicious activity.
Attackers might leverage this in order to conduct data destruction or data encrypted for impact on the data stores of services like Exchange and SQL Server.
falsepositives: Expected FP with some processes using this techniques to terminate one of their processes during installations and updates
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\taskkill.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='taskkill.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -f %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /f %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –f %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —f %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―f %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -f' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /f' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –f' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —f' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―f' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -im %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /im %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –im %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —im %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―im %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -pid %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /pid %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –pid %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —pid %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―pid %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\Temp%' ESCAPE '\') AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%.tmp' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Process Terminated Via Taskkill

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to shell context menu commands. Use this rule to hunt for potential anomalies and suspicious shell commands.
falsepositives: Likely from new software installation suggesting to add context menu items. Such as "PowerShell", "Everything", "Git", etc.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Software\\Classes\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\shell\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\command\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Shell Context Menu Command Tampering

author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the "net" utility.
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behaviour in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '% stop %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Stop Windows Service Via Net.EXE

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may attempt to find domain-level groups and permission settings.
The knowledge of domain-level permission groups can help adversaries determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group.
Adversaries may use this information to determine which users have elevated permissions, such as domain administrators.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership%' ESCAPE '\' OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-aduser%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-f %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-pr %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%DoesNotRequirePreAuth%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: AD Groups Or Users Enumeration Using PowerShell - ScriptBlock

author: frack113
description: Detects usage of the "Get-AdGroup" cmdlet to enumerate Groups within Active Directory
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-AdGroup %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Filter%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Active Directory Group Enumeration With Get-AdGroup

author: frack113
description: Detects when a powershell script contains calls to the "New-NetFirewallRule" cmdlet in order to add a new firewall rule with an "Allow" action.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%New-NetFirewallRule%-Action%Allow%' ESCAPE '\')
title: New Windows Firewall Rule Added Via New-NetFirewallRule Cmdlet - ScriptBlock

author: Arun Chauhan
description: Detects nltest commands that can be used for information discovery
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\nltest.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='nltestrk.exe'))
title: Nltest.EXE Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects potential suspicious execution of a GUID like folder name located in a suspicious location such as %TEMP% as seen being used in IcedID attacks.
Use this rule to hunt for potentially suspicious activity stemming from uncommon folders.
falsepositives: Installers are sometimes known for creating temporary folders with GUID like names. Add appropriate filters accordingly
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((CommandLine LIKE '%\\AppData\\Roaming\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%\\{%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%}\\%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\{%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%}\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR NewProcessName IS NULL OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\drvinst.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR (NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\msiexec.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\msiexec.exe' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Potential Suspicious Execution From GUID Like Folder Names

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to the "ExtErrorInformation" key in order to disable ETW logging for rpcrt4.dll
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\Rpc\\ExtErrorInformation' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewValue='DWORD (0x00000000)' OR NewValue='DWORD (0x00000002)')))
title: ETW Logging Disabled For rpcrt4.dll

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects disabling of the "Automatic Sample Submission" feature of Windows Defender.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' AND (EventID=5007 AND NewValue LIKE '%\\Real-Time Protection\\SubmitSamplesConsent = 0x0%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Windows Defender Submit Sample Feature Disabled

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the creation of scheduled tasks by user accounts via the "schtasks" utility.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% /create %' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((User LIKE '%AUTHORI%' ESCAPE '\' OR User LIKE '%AUTORI%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\root\\integration\\integrator.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft Office\\root\\integration\\integrator.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%Microsoft\\Office\\Office Performance Monitor%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Scheduled Task Creation Via Schtasks.EXE

author: Center for Threat Informed Defense (CTID) Summiting the Pyramid Team
description: Detects the creation of a scheduled task via Registry keys.
falsepositives: Likely as this is a normal behaviour on Windows
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND (OperationType='New registry value created' OR OperationType='Existing registry value modified')) AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Schedule\\TaskCache\\Tasks\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\Schedule\\TaskCache\\Tree\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Scheduled Task Created - Registry

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may look for folders and drives shared on remote systems as a means of identifying sources of information to gather as
a precursor for Collection and to identify potential systems of interest for Lateral Movement.
Networks often contain shared network drives and folders that enable users to access file directories on various systems across a network.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-smbshare%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Suspicious Get Information for SMB Share

author: vburov
description: Detect suspicious parent processes of well-known Windows processes
falsepositives: Some security products seem to spawn these
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\taskhost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\lsm.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\lsass.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\services.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\lsaiso.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\csrss.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wininit.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\winlogon.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\SavService.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\ngen.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\Windows Defender\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\Microsoft Security Client\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (ParentProcessName IS NULL OR (ParentProcessName='' OR ParentProcessName='-'))), 0))))
title: Windows Processes Suspicious Parent Directory

author: frack113
description: Detects Set-Alias or New-Alias cmdlet usage. Which can be use as a mean to obfuscate PowerShell scripts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Set-Alias %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%New-Alias %' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name ncms -Value New-CimSession -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name gcls -Value Get-CimClass -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name ncso -Value New-CimSessionOption -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name gcms -Value Get-CimSession -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name rcms -Value Remove-cimSession -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name rcie -Value Register-CimIndicationEvent -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name gcai -Value Get-CimAssociatedInstance -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name gcim -Value Get-CimInstance -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name scim -Value Set-CimInstance -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name ncim -Value New-CimInstance -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name ncim -Value New-CimInstance  -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name rcim -Value Remove-cimInstance -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue' OR ScriptBlockText='Set-Alias -Name icim -Value Invoke-CimMethod -Option ReadOnly, AllScope -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue'), 0))))
title: Potential PowerShell Obfuscation Using Alias Cmdlets

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects logons using NTLM, which could be caused by a legacy source or attackers
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational' AND EventID=8002
title: NTLM Logon

author: @SerkinValery
description:
Detects denied requests by Active Directory Certificate Services.
Example of these requests denial include issues with permissions on the certificate template or invalid signatures.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND (Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-CertificationAuthority' AND EventID=53)
title: Active Directory Certificate Services Denied Certificate Enrollment Request

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects modification of dMSA link attributes (msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink) via PowerShell scripts.
This command line pattern could be an indicator an attempt to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server 2025.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrative tasks modifying these attributes.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%.Put("msDS-ManagedAccountPrecededByLink%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%CN=%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: DMSA Link Attributes Modified

author: Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Ian Davis, oscd.community
description: Detects the installation of a well-known TAP driver service. This could be a sign of potential preparation for data exfiltration using tunnelling techniques.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4697 AND ServiceFileName LIKE '%tap0901%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Tap Driver Installation - Security

author: Furkan CALISKAN, @caliskanfurkan_, @oscd_initiative
description:
Detects the creation of a child "explorer.exe" process from a shell like process such as "cmd.exe" or "powershell.exe".
Attackers can use "explorer.exe" for evading defense mechanisms by proxying the execution through the latter.
While this is often a legitimate action, this rule can be use to hunt for anomalies.
Muddy Waters threat actor was seeing using this technique.
falsepositives: Legitimate explorer.exe run from a shell host like "cmd.exe" or "powershell.exe"
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%explorer.exe%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potential Proxy Execution Via Explorer.EXE From Shell Process

author: frack113, Christopher Peacock '@securepeacock', SCYTHE '@scythe_io'
description: Adversaries may look for details about the network configuration and settings of systems they access or through information discovery of remote systems
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine REGEXP 'ipconfig\s+/all' OR CommandLine REGEXP 'netsh\s+interface show interface' OR CommandLine REGEXP 'arp\s+-a' OR CommandLine REGEXP 'nbtstat\s+-n' OR CommandLine REGEXP 'net\s+config' OR CommandLine REGEXP 'route\s+print'))
title: Suspicious Network Command

author: Josh Nickels, Qi Nan
description:
Detects the command line executed when TeamViewer starts a session started by a remote host.
Once a connection has been started, an investigator can verify the connection details by viewing the "incoming_connections.txt" log file in the TeamViewer folder.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE 'TeamViewer\_Desktop.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentProcessName LIKE 'TeamViewer\_Service.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%TeamViewer\_Desktop.exe --IPCport 5939 --Module 1' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Remote Access Tool - Team Viewer Session Started On Windows Host

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects Windows services that got terminated for whatever reason
falsepositives: False positives could occur since service termination could happen due to multiple reasons
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND (Provider_Name='Service Control Manager' AND EventID=7023)
title: Windows Service Terminated With Error

author: frack113
description: Get the processes that are running on the local computer.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-Process%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Suspicious Process Discovery With Get-Process

author: Michael Haag, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects execution of Advanced Installer MSIX Package Support Framework (PSF) components, specifically AI_STUBS executables with original filename 'popupwrapper.exe'.
This activity may indicate malicious MSIX packages build with Advanced Installer leveraging the Package Support Framework to bypass application control restrictions.
falsepositives: Legitimate applications packaged with Advanced Installer using Package Support Framework
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AI\_STUBS\\AiStubX64Elevated.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AI\_STUBS\\AiStubX86Elevated.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AI\_STUBS\\AiStubX64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AI\_STUBS\\AiStubX86.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND OriginalFileName='popupwrapper.exe'))
title: Windows MSIX Package Support Framework AI_STUBS Execution

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system they are currently accessing or from remote systems by querying for information over the network.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND ContextInfo LIKE '%Get-NetTCPConnection%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Use Get-NetTCPConnection - PowerShell Module

author: @SerkinValery
description:
Detects errors when a target server doesn't have suitable keys for generating kerberos tickets.
This issue can occur for example when a service uses a user account or a computer account that is configured for only DES encryption on a computer that is running Windows 7 which has DES encryption for Kerberos authentication disabled.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND ((Provider_Name='Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center' OR Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-Kerberos-Key-Distribution-Center') AND (EventID=16 OR EventID=27))
title: No Suitable Encryption Key Found For Generating Kerberos Ticket

author: Ali Alwashali
description: Detects the execution of a system command via the ScreenConnect RMM service.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of ScreenConnect. Disable this rule if ScreenConnect is heavily used.
