rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\TEMP\\ScreenConnect\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Remote Access Tool - ScreenConnect Remote Command Execution

author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime
description: Detects activity when a security-enabled global group is deleted
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4730 OR EventID=634)
title: A Security-Enabled Global Group Was Deleted

author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
description: Identifies use of various commands to query a systems time. This technique may be used before executing a scheduled task or to discover the time zone of a target system.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the system utilities to discover system time for legitimate reason
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%time%' ESCAPE '\') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\w32tm.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%tz%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Discovery of a System Time

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may attempt to gather information about attached peripheral devices and components connected to a computer system.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Win32\_PnPEntity%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Powershell Suspicious Win32_PnPEntity

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of network connections to or from the compromised system they are currently accessing or from remote systems by querying for information over the network.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Windows PowerShell' AND (EventID=400 AND Data LIKE '%Get-NetTCPConnection%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Use Get-NetTCPConnection

author: frack113
description: Detect the usage of "DirLister.exe" a utility for quickly listing folder or drive contents. It was seen used by BlackCat ransomware to create a list of accessible directories and files.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (OriginalFileName='DirLister.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\DirLister.exe' ESCAPE '\'))
title: DirLister Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of 7zip utilities (7z.exe, 7za.exe and 7zr.exe) to extract password protected zip files.
falsepositives: Legitimate activity is expected since extracting files with a password can be common in some environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((Description LIKE '%7-Zip%' ESCAPE '\' OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\7z.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\7za.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\7zr.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='7z.exe' OR OriginalFileName='7za.exe' OR OriginalFileName='7zr.exe')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -p%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% x %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% -o%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Password Protected Compressed File Extraction Via 7Zip

author: frack113
description: PowerShell Remove-Item  with -Path to delete a file or a folder with "-Recurse"
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Remove-Item -Path %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%del -Path %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%erase -Path %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%rd -Path %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ri -Path %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%rm -Path %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%rmdir -Path %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Use Of Remove-Item to Delete File - ScriptBlock

author: A. Sungurov , oscd.community
description: Detect indirect command execution via Program Compatibility Assistant pcwrun.exe
falsepositives: Need to use extra processing with 'unique_count' / 'filter' to focus on outliers as opposed to commonly seen artifacts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\pcwrun.exe' ESCAPE '\')
title: Indirect Command Execution By Program Compatibility Wizard

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects execution of JavaScript or JSC files using NodeJs binary node.exe, that could be potentially suspicious.
Node.js is a popular open-source JavaScript runtime that runs code outside browsers and is widely used for both frontend and backend development.
Adversaries have been observed abusing Node.js to disguise malware as legitimate processes, evade security defenses, and maintain persistence within target systems.
Because Node.js is commonly used, this rule may generate false positives in some environments. However, if such activity is unusual in your environment, it is highly suspicious and warrants immediate investigation.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of node.exe to execute JavaScript or JSC files on your environment
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\node.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='node.exe' OR Product='Node.js') AND CommandLine LIKE '%.js%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: NodeJS Execution of JavaScript File

author: Janantha Marasinghe
description: Adversaries can carry out malicious operations using a virtual instance to avoid detection. This rule is built to detect the registration of the Virtualbox driver or start of a Virtualbox VM.
falsepositives: This may have false positives on hosts where Virtualbox is legitimately being used for operations
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%VBoxRT.dll,RTR3Init%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%VBoxC.dll%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%VBoxDrv.sys%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%startvm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%controlvm%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Virtualbox Driver Installation or Starting of VMs

author: frack113
description:
Detects when an executable launches an identical instance of itself, a behavior often used to create a suspended “sacrificial” process for code injection or evasion.
Investigate for indicators such as the process being started in suspended mode, rapid parent termination, memory manipulation (e.g., WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread), or unsigned binaries.
Review command-line arguments, process ancestry, and network activity to confirm if this is legitimate behavior or process injection activity.
falsepositives: Legitimate software that may launch a new instance of itself, especially updaters or installers. Investigate each alert and apply whitelisting as needed.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName=ParentProcessName AND (NOT COALESCE(((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe' OR OriginalFileName='CompatTelRunner.exe' OR OriginalFileName='Discord.exe' OR OriginalFileName='electron.exe' OR OriginalFileName='EXPLORER.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='httpd.exe' OR OriginalFileName='IE4UINIT.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='mmc.exe' OR OriginalFileName='MpCmdRun.exe' OR OriginalFileName='mscorsvw.exe' OR OriginalFileName='msiexec.exe' OR OriginalFileName='NGenTask.exe' OR OriginalFileName='OneDriveSetup.exe' OR OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='REGSVR32.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='smss.exe' OR OriginalFileName='Spotify.exe' OR OriginalFileName='WerMgr') OR (Product='Avira' OR Product='Evernote' OR Product='Firefox' OR Product='Microsoft Office' OR Product='Ninite' OR Product='Opera Browser Assistant Installer' OR Product='Opera Installer' OR Product='Sysinternals Sysmon')), 0))))
title: Potential Executable Run Itself As Sacrificial Process

author: frack113
description: Detects the execution of "attrib" with the "+s" flag to mark files as system files
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\attrib.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='ATTRIB.EXE') AND CommandLine LIKE '% +s %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Set Files as System Files Using Attrib.EXE

author: frack113
description: Detetcts PowerShell activity in which Get-Addefaultdomainpasswordpolicy is used to get the default password policy for an Active Directory domain.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-AdDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Password Policy Discovery With Get-AdDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects a curl process start on Windows, which could indicates a file download from a remote location or a simple web request to a remote server
falsepositives: Scripts created by developers and admins
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\curl.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Product='The curl executable'))
title: Curl.EXE Execution

author: AdmU3
description:
Detects execution of "tar.exe" in order to extract compressed file.
Adversaries may abuse various utilities in order to decompress data to avoid detection.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\tar.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='bsdtar') AND CommandLine LIKE '%-x%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Compressed File Extraction Via Tar.EXE

author: Timur Zinniatullin, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community
description: Detects the creation of a new service using powershell.
falsepositives: Legitimate administrator or user creates a service for legitimate reasons.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%New-Service%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-BinaryPathName%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: New Service Creation Using PowerShell

author: Alexandr Yampolskyi, SOC Prime
description: Detects activity when a member is added to a security-enabled global group
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4728 OR EventID=632)
title: A Member Was Added to a Security-Enabled Global Group

author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the stopping of a Windows service via the PowerShell Cmdlet "Stop-Service"
falsepositives: There are many legitimate reasons to stop a service. This rule isn't looking for any suspicious behaviour in particular. Filter legitimate activity accordingly
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%Stop-Service %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Stop Windows Service Via PowerShell Stop-Service

author: frack113
description:
An adversary may deface systems internal to an organization in an attempt to intimidate or mislead users.
This may take the form of modifications to internal websites, or directly to user systems with the replacement of the desktop wallpaper
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-ItemProperty%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Registry::%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%HKEY\_CURRENT\_USER\\Control Panel\\Desktop\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%WallPaper%' ESCAPE '\') OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%SystemParametersInfo(20,0,%,3)%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Replace Desktop Wallpaper by Powershell

author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects PowerShell scripts set ACL to of a file or a folder
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Set-Acl %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-AclObject %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Path %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: PowerShell Script Change Permission Via Set-Acl - PsScript

author: oscd.community, @redcanary, Zach Stanford @svch0st
description: Detects when when a mounted share is removed. Adversaries may remove share connections that are no longer useful in order to clean up traces of their operation
falsepositives: Administrators or Power users may remove their shares via cmd line
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%share%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/delete%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Unmount Share Via Net.EXE

author: Teymur Kheirkhabarov (idea), Vasiliy Burov (rule), oscd.community, Tim Shelton
description: Detects specific combinations of encoding methods in PowerShell via the commandline
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll')) AND (((CommandLine LIKE '%ToInt%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ToDecimal%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ToByte%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ToUint%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ToSingle%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ToSByte%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%ToChar%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ToString%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%String%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((CommandLine LIKE '%char%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%join%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%split%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%join%' ESCAPE '\')))))
title: Potential Encoded PowerShell Patterns In CommandLine

author: frack113
description:
Detects the use of PowerShell modules and cmdlets to gather local group information.
Adversaries may use local system permission groups to determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group such as the local administrators group.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND (((Payload LIKE '%get-localgroup %' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%get-localgroupmember %' ESCAPE '\') OR (ContextInfo LIKE '%get-localgroup %' ESCAPE '\' OR ContextInfo LIKE '%get-localgroupmember %' ESCAPE '\')) OR (((Payload LIKE '%get-wmiobject %' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%gwmi %' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%get-ciminstance %' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%gcim %' ESCAPE '\') OR (ContextInfo LIKE '%get-wmiobject %' ESCAPE '\' AND ContextInfo LIKE '%gwmi %' ESCAPE '\' AND ContextInfo LIKE '%get-ciminstance %' ESCAPE '\' AND ContextInfo LIKE '%gcim %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (Payload LIKE '%win32\_group%' ESCAPE '\' OR ContextInfo LIKE '%win32\_group%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Suspicious Get Local Groups Information

author: oscd.community, Natalia Shornikova
description: Detects unusually long PowerShell command lines with a length of 1000 characters or more
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll') OR Description='Windows Powershell' OR Product='PowerShell Core 6') AND CommandLine REGEXP '.{1000,}'))
title: Unusually Long PowerShell CommandLine

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects execution of Sysinternals tools via an AppX package.
Attackers could install the Sysinternals Suite to get access to tools such as psexec and procdump to avoid detection based on System paths.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of sysinternals applications from the Windows Store will trigger this. Apply exclusions as needed.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin' AND (EventID=201 AND (ImageName='procdump.exe' OR ImageName='psloglist.exe' OR ImageName='psexec.exe' OR ImageName='livekd.exe' OR ImageName='ADExplorer.exe'))
title: Sysinternals Tools AppX Versions Execution

author: frack113
description: Detects PowerShell scripts leveraging the "Invoke-WebRequest" cmdlet to send data via either "PUT" or "POST" method.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Invoke-RestMethod%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Invoke-WebRequest%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%irm %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%iwr %' ESCAPE '\') AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Method "POST"%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Method "PUT"%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Method POST%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Method PUT%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Method ''POST''%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Method ''PUT''%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PowerShell Script With File Upload Capabilities

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
description:
Detects a CodePage modification using the "mode.com" utility.
This behavior has been used by threat actors behind Dharma ransomware.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\mode.com' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='MODE.COM') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% con %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% cp %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% select=%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: CodePage Modification Via MODE.COM

author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
description:
Detects the use of the WMI command-line (WMIC) utility to identify and display various system information,
including OS, CPU, GPU, disk drive names, memory capacity, display resolution, baseboard, BIOS,
and GPU driver products/versions.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((Description='WMI Commandline Utility' OR OriginalFileName='wmic.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\WMIC.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%get%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%baseboard%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%bios%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cpu%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%diskdrive%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%logicaldisk%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%memphysical%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%os%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%path%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%startup%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%win32\_videocontroller%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%caption%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%command%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%driverversion%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%maxcapacity%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%name%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%osarchitecture%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%product%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%size%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%smbiosbiosversion%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%version%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%videomodedescription%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((ParentCommandLine LIKE '%\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\serviceDiscovery\\scripts\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: System Information Discovery Via Wmic.EXE

author: frack113
description: Detects modification of the registry settings used for Internet Explorer and other Windows components that use these settings. An attacker can abuse this registry key to add a domain to the trusted sites Zone or insert JavaScript for persistence
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Internet Settings%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewValue LIKE 'DWORD%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue IS NULL OR (NewValue='Cookie:' OR NewValue='Visited:' OR NewValue='(Empty)') OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Cache%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\ZoneMap%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\WpadDecision%' ESCAPE '\') OR NewValue='Binary Data'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetObject LIKE '%\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Internet Settings\\Accepted Documents%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Modification of IE Registry Settings

author: frack113
description: Detects the execution of clip.exe in order to copy data to the clipboard. Adversaries may collect data stored in the clipboard from users copying information within or between applications.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\clip.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='clip.exe'))
title: Data Copied To Clipboard Via Clip.EXE

author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects logon events that specify new credentials
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND LogonType=9)
title: Outgoing Logon with New Credentials

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may enumerate browser bookmarks to learn more about compromised hosts.
Browser bookmarks may reveal personal information about users (ex: banking sites, interests, social media, etc.) as well as details about
internal network resources such as servers, tools/dashboards, or other related infrastructure.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-ChildItem%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '% -Recurse %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '% -Path %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '% -Filter Bookmarks%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '% -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '% -Force%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Automated Collection Bookmarks Using Get-ChildItem PowerShell

author: Muhammad Faisal (@faisalusuf)
description: Detects the execution of Microsoft Quick Assist tool "QuickAssist.exe". This utility can be used by attackers to gain remote access.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Quick Assist in the environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\QuickAssist.exe' ESCAPE '\')
title: QuickAssist Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects specific techniques often seen used inside of PowerShell scripts to obfscuate Alias creation
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Alias%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '% -Value (-join(%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potential PowerShell Obfuscation Using Character Join

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
description:
Detects the enumeration and query of interesting and in some cases sensitive services on the system via "sc.exe".
Attackers often try to enumerate the services currently running on a system in order to find different attack vectors.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='sc.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '%query%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%termservice%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Interesting Service Enumeration Via Sc.EXE

author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io
description: Detects execution of "Get-NetFirewallRule" or "Show-NetFirewallRule" to enumerate the local firewall rules on a host.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND ((Payload LIKE '%Get-NetFirewallRule%' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%Show-NetFirewallRule%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ContextInfo LIKE '%Get-NetFirewallRule%' ESCAPE '\' OR ContextInfo LIKE '%Show-NetFirewallRule%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Local Firewall Rules Enumeration Via NetFirewallRule Cmdlet

author: frack113
description: Detect use of Get-GPO to get one GPO or all the GPOs in a domain.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-GPO%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Suspicious GPO Discovery With Get-GPO

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of Chromium based browser in headless mode
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\brave.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\chrome.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msedge.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\opera.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\vivaldi.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%--headless%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Browser Execution In Headless Mode

author: Oddvar Moe, Sander Wiebing, oscd.community
description: Detects the export of the target Registry key to a file.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regedit.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='REGEDIT.EXE') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -E %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /E %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –E %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —E %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―E %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((CommandLine LIKE '%hklm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%hkey\_local\_machine%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%\\system' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\sam' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\security' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Exports Registry Key To a File

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects when a share is mounted using the "net.exe" utility
falsepositives: Legitimate activity by administrators and scripts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\net1.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='net.exe' OR OriginalFileName='net1.exe')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '% use %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% \\\\%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Windows Share Mount Via Net.EXE

author: Tom3306
description: Detects AppLocker policy enumeration attempts via PowerShell using the Get-AppLockerPolicy cmdlet and an policy scope of either Effective, LDAP, or Local.
falsepositives: PowerShell-based AppLocker auditing and policy troubleshooting by administrators.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%Get-AppLockerPolicy%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -Effective%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /Effective%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –Effective%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —Effective%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―Effective%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -Ldap %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /Ldap %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –Ldap %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —Ldap %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―Ldap %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -Local%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /Local%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –Local%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —Local%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―Local%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PowerShell AppLocker Policy Discovery Via Get-AppLockerPolicy

author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g (rule), oscd.community (improvements)
description: Detects non-interactive PowerShell activity by looking at the "powershell" process with a non-user GUI process such as "explorer.exe" as a parent.
falsepositives: Likely. Many admin scripts and tools leverage PowerShell in their BAT or VB scripts which may trigger this rule often. It is best to add additional filters or use this to hunt for anomalies
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\CompatTelRunner.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR ParentProcessName LIKE ':\\$WINDOWS.~BT\\Sources\\SetupHost.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\Microsoft VS Code\\Code.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentCommandLine LIKE '% --ms-enable-electron-run-as-node %' ESCAPE '\') OR (ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal\_%' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\WindowsTerminal.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection\\SenseIR.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Non Interactive PowerShell Process Spawned

author: Roberto Rodriguez @Cyb3rWard0g, Open Threat Research (OTR)
description: Detects volume shadow copy mount via Windows event log
falsepositives: Legitimate use of volume shadow copy mounts (backups maybe).
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='System' AND (Provider_Name='Microsoft-Windows-Ntfs' AND EventID=98 AND DeviceName LIKE '%HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Volume Shadow Copy Mount

author: frack113
description: Use of reg to get MachineGuid information
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Cryptography%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/v %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%MachineGuid%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Query of MachineGUID

author: Keith Wright
description: Detects external disk drives or plugged-in USB devices.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=6416 AND (ClassName='DiskDrive' OR DeviceDescription='USB Mass Storage Device'))
title: External Disk Drive Or USB Storage Device Was Recognized By The System

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects attempted file load events that did not meet the signing level requirements. It often means the file's signature is revoked or a signature with the Lifetime Signing EKU has expired.
This event is best correlated with EID 3089 to determine the error of the validation.
falsepositives: Antivirus and other third party products are known to trigger this rule quite a lot. Initial filters and tuning is required before using this rule.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity/Operational' AND ((EventID=3033 OR EventID=3034) AND (NOT COALESCE((FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\assembly\\GAC\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\mscorsvw.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\Microsoft.NET\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=8), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\DTrace\\dtrace.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=12) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\DriverStore\\FileRepository\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\igd10iumd64.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=7) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\nvspcap64.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND (ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Keybase\\Gui\\Keybase.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Teams\\stage\\Teams.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND RequestedPolicy=8) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\Bonjour\\mdnsNSP.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND (ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\SIHClient.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (RequestedPolicy=8 OR RequestedPolicy=12)) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Microsoft Office\\root\\vfs\\ProgramFilesCommonX64\\Microsoft Shared\\OFFICE%' ESCAPE '\' AND FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\MSOXMLMF.DLL' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=7) OR (ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\Microsoft Office\\root\\vfs\\ProgramFilesCommonX64\\Microsoft Shared\\Office%' ESCAPE '\' AND FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=8) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\System32\\nvspcap64.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\slack\\app-%' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\slack.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=8) OR ((FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Mozilla Firefox\\mozavcodec.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Mozilla Firefox\\mozavutil.dll' ESCAPE '\') AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Mozilla Firefox\\firefox.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=8) OR ((FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\Avast Software\\Avast\\aswAMSI.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files (x86)\\Avast Software\\Avast\\aswAMSI.dll' ESCAPE '\') AND (RequestedPolicy=8 OR RequestedPolicy=12)) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\Google\\Drive File Stream\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\crashpad\_handler.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Windows\\ImmersiveControlPanel\\SystemSettings.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=8) OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Trend Micro\\Client Server Security Agent\\perficrcperfmonmgr.dll' ESCAPE '\' AND RequestedPolicy=8) OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\National Instruments\\Shared\\mDNS Responder\\nimdnsNSP.dll ' ESCAPE '\' OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\McAfee\\Endpoint Security\\Threat Prevention\\MfeAmsiProvider.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\McAfee\\MfeAV\\AMSIExt.dll' ESCAPE '\') OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\ESET\\ESET Security\\eamsi.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\comodo\\comodo internet security\\amsiprovider\_x64.dll' ESCAPE '\' OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\SentinelOne\\Sentinel Agent%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Program Files\\SentinelOne\\Sentinel Agent%' ESCAPE '\') OR FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\National Instruments\\Shared\\mDNS Responder\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ((ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Kaspersky Lab\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ProcessNameBuffer LIKE '%\\avp.exe%' ESCAPE '\') OR (FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\Kaspersky Lab\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND FileNameBuffer LIKE '%\\antimalware\_provider.dll%' ESCAPE '\'))), 0)))
title: CodeIntegrity - Unmet Signing Level Requirements By File Under Validation

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects execution of processes with image paths starting with WebDAV shares (\\), which might indicate malicious file execution from remote web shares.
Execution of processes from WebDAV shares can be a sign of lateral movement or exploitation attempts, especially if the process is not a known legitimate application.
Exploitation Attempt of vulnerabilities like CVE-2025-33053 also involves executing processes from WebDAV paths.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of WebDAV shares for process execution
Known applications executing from WebDAV paths
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '\\\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\DavWWWRoot\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Process Execution From WebDAV Share

author: Ahmed Farouk, Nasreddine Bencherchali
description:
Detects execution of commands via the run dialog box on Windows by checking values of the "RunMRU" registry key.
This technique was seen being abused by threat actors to deceive users into pasting and executing malicious commands, often disguised as CAPTCHA verification steps.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\RunMRU%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetObject LIKE '%\\MRUList' ESCAPE '\'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((NewValue LIKE '%ping%' ESCAPE '\' OR (NewValue LIKE '\%appdata\%\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '\%localappdata\%\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '\%public\%\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '\%temp\%\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'calc\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'dxdiag\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'explorer\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'gpedit.msc\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'mmc\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'notepad\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'regedit\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'services.msc\\1' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE 'winver\\1' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Command Executed Via Run Dialog Box - Registry

author: frack113
description:
Detects the use of PowerShell modules and cmdlets to gather local group information.
Adversaries may use local system permission groups to determine which groups exist and which users belong to a particular group such as the local administrators group.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-localgroup %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-localgroupmember %' ESCAPE '\') OR ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-wmiobject %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%gwmi %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%get-ciminstance %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%gcim %' ESCAPE '\') AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%win32\_group%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Get Local Groups Information - PowerShell

author: @neu5ron
description: Detect scenarios where a potentially unauthorized application or user is modifying the system time.
falsepositives: HyperV or other virtualization technologies with binary not listed in filter portion of detection
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4616 AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND SubjectUserSid='S-1-5-19'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\vmtoolsd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\VMware\\VMware Tools\\vmtoolsd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\VBoxService.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\oobe\\msoobe.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Unauthorized System Time Modification

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to the registry values related to outlook that indicates that a reminder was triggered for a Note or Task item. This could be a sign of exploitation of CVE-2023-23397. Further investigation is required to determine the success of an exploitation.
falsepositives: Legitimate reminders received for a task or a note will also trigger this rule.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Office\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Outlook\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Tasks\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Notes\\%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Outlook Task/Note Reminder Received

author: frack113
description: Detects the creation of a new bits job by PowerShell
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Bits-Client/Operational' AND (EventID=3 AND (processPath LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR processPath LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\'))
title: New BITS Job Created Via PowerShell

author: Daniel Degasperi '@d4ns4n_'
description: Detects the invocation of MS SQL transactions that are destructive towards table or database data, such as "DROP TABLE" or "DROP DATABASE".
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name='MSSQLSERVER$AUDIT' AND EventID=33205 AND (Data LIKE '%statement:TRUNCATE TABLE%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%statement:DROP TABLE%' ESCAPE '\' OR Data LIKE '%statement:DROP DATABASE%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: MSSQL Destructive Query

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the extraction of password protected ZIP archives. See the filename variable for more details on which file has been opened.
falsepositives: Legitimate used of encrypted ZIP files
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=5379 AND TargetName LIKE '%Microsoft\_Windows\_Shell\_ZipFolder:filename%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((TargetName LIKE '%\\Temporary Internet Files\\Content.Outlook%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Password Protected ZIP File Opened

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Cedric MAURUGEON (Update)
description: Detects the execution of the "curl" process with "upload" flags. Which might indicate potential data exfiltration
falsepositives: Scripts created by developers and admins
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\curl.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR Product='The curl executable') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '% --form%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% --upload-file %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% --data %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% --data-%' ESCAPE '\') OR CommandLine REGEXP '\s-[FTd]\s')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%://localhost%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%://127.0.0.1%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Potential Data Exfiltration Via Curl.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the launch of a child process via "conhost.exe" with the "--headless" flag.
The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\conhost.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentCommandLine LIKE '%--headless%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Headless Process Launched Via Conhost.EXE

author: Agro (@agro_sev) oscd.community
description:
This rule detects execution of a PowerShell code through the sqlps.exe utility, which is included in the standard set of utilities supplied with the MSSQL Server.
Script blocks are not logged in this case, so this utility helps to bypass protection mechanisms based on the analysis of these logs.
falsepositives: Direct PS command execution through SQLPS.exe is uncommon, childprocess sqlps.exe spawned by sqlagent.exe is a legitimate action.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\sqlps.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sqlps.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='sqlps.exe') AND (NOT COALESCE((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\sqlagent.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))))
title: Detection of PowerShell Execution via Sqlps.exe

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of Dsacls to grant over permissive permissions
falsepositives: Legitimate administrators granting over permissive permissions to users
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\dsacls.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='DSACLS.EXE') AND CommandLine LIKE '% /G %' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%GR%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%GE%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%GW%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%GA%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%WP%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%WD%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potentially Over Permissive Permissions Granted Using Dsacls.EXE

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects an uncommon svchost parent process
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\svchost.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\Mrt.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\MsMpEng.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\ngen.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\rpcnet.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\services.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\TiWorker.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR ParentProcessName IS NULL OR (ParentProcessName='-' OR ParentProcessName='')), 0))))
title: Uncommon Svchost Parent Process

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the creation of a dMSA service account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server 2025.
On top of that, if the user that is creating the dMSASvc account is not a legitimate administrator or does not have the necessary permissions,
it is a strong signal of an attempted or successful abuse of the BaDSuccessor vulnerability for privilege escalation within the Windows Server 2025 Active Directory environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%New-ADServiceAccount%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-CreateDelegatedServiceAccount%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-path%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs - PowerShell

author: Syed Hasan (@syedhasan009)
description: Detects the mount of an ISO image on an endpoint
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4663 AND ObjectServer='Security' AND ObjectType='File' AND ObjectName LIKE '\\Device\\CdRom%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((ObjectName LIKE '\\Device\\CdRom0\\autorun.ico' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '\\Device\\CdRom0\\setup.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ObjectName LIKE '\\Device\\CdRom0\\setup64.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: ISO Image Mounted

author: Thomas Patzke
description: Addition of domains is seldom and should be verified for legitimacy.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND EventID=4706
title: A New Trust Was Created To A Domain

author: frack113
description:
Detects execution of Windows Defender "OfflineScannerShell.exe" from its non standard directory.
The "OfflineScannerShell.exe" binary is vulnerable to DLL side loading and will load any DLL named "mpclient.dll" from the current working directory.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\OfflineScannerShell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='OfflineScannerShell.exe') AND (NOT COALESCE((CurrentDirectory LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\Offline\\' ESCAPE '\' OR CurrentDirectory='' OR CurrentDirectory IS NULL), 0))))
title: Potential Mpclient.DLL Sideloading Via OfflineScannerShell.EXE Execution

author: frack113
description: Detects usage of COM objects that can be abused to download files in PowerShell by CLSID
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%[Type]::GetTypeFromCLSID(%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%0002DF01-0000-0000-C000-000000000046%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%F6D90F16-9C73-11D3-B32E-00C04F990BB4%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%F5078F35-C551-11D3-89B9-0000F81FE221%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%88d96a0a-f192-11d4-a65f-0040963251e5%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%AFBA6B42-5692-48EA-8141-DC517DCF0EF1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%AFB40FFD-B609-40A3-9828-F88BBE11E4E3%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%88d96a0b-f192-11d4-a65f-0040963251e5%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%2087c2f4-2cef-4953-a8ab-66779b670495%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%000209FF-0000-0000-C000-000000000046%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%00024500-0000-0000-C000-000000000046%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential COM Objects Download Cradles Usage - Process Creation

author: Michaela Adams, Zach Mathis
description: Detects potential token impersonation and theft. Example, when using "DuplicateToken(Ex)" and "ImpersonateLoggedOnUser" with the "LOGON32_LOGON_NEW_CREDENTIALS flag".
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4624 AND LogonType=9 AND LogonProcessName='Advapi' AND AuthenticationPackageName='Negotiate' AND ImpersonationLevel LIKE '\%\%1833' ESCAPE '\')
title: Potential Access Token Abuse

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of "TroubleshootingPack" cmdlets to leverage CVE-2022-30190 or action similar to "msdt" lolbin (as described in LOLBAS)
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of "TroubleshootingPack" cmdlet for troubleshooting purposes
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Invoke-TroubleshootingPack%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%C:\\Windows\\Diagnostics\\System\\PCW%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-AnswerFile%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Unattended%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Troubleshooting Pack Cmdlet Execution

author: frack113
description: Detects registry modifications that disable Privacy Settings Experience
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\OOBE\\DisablePrivacyExperience' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000000)'))
title: Disable Privacy Settings Experience in Registry

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of Gpg4win to decrypt files
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\gpg.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\gpg2.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR Description='GnuPG’s OpenPGP tool') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -d %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%passphrase%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: File Decryption Using Gpg4win

author: frack113
description: Detects the use of a Microsoft signed script executing a managed DLL with PowerShell.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%UtilityFunctions.ps1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%RegSnapin %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: UtilityFunctions.ps1 Proxy Dll

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects when an attacker tries to add a new network provider in order to dump clear text credentials, similar to how the NPPSpy tool does it
falsepositives: Other legitimate network providers used and not filtred in this rule
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\NetworkProvider%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE(((TargetObject LIKE '%\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\WebClient\\NetworkProvider%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\LanmanWorkstation\\NetworkProvider%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\RDPNP\\NetworkProvider%' ESCAPE '\') OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\poqexec.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Potential Credential Dumping Attempt Using New NetworkProvider - REG

author: Marco Pedrinazzi (@pedrinazziM) (InTheCyber)
description:
Detects inbox rule creation or update via ExchangePowerShell cmdlet, a technique commonly observed in Business Email Compromise (BEC) attacks to hide emails.
The usage of inbox rules can be a sign of a compromised mailbox, where an attacker is attempting to evade detections by suppressing or redirecting incoming emails.
Analysts should review these rules in context, validate whether they reflect normal user behavior, and correlate with other indicators such as unusual login activity or recent mailbox rule modifications.
falsepositives: Legitimate inbox rules created by users or administrators to manage email flow such as filtering, organizing, or automating email handling.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%New-InboxRule%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Set-InboxRule%' ESCAPE '\') AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%DeleteMessage%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%MarkAsRead%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%MoveToFolder%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%SubjectOrBodyContainsWords%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Inbox Rules Creation Or Update Activity Via ExchangePowerShell Cmdlet

author: Victor Sergeev, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, Gleb Sukhodolskiy, Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Tim Shelton, frack113 (split)
description: Detects modification of autostart extensibility point (ASEP) in registry.
falsepositives: Legitimate software automatically (mostly, during installation) sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
Legitimate administrator sets up autorun keys for legitimate reason
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager%' ESCAPE '\' AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\SetupExecute%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\S0InitialCommand%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\KnownDlls%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Execute%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\BootExecute%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\AppCertDlls%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewValue='(Empty)'), 0))))
title: Session Manager Autorun Keys Modification

author: Austin Songer
description:
Detects when a user enables DNS-over-HTTPS.
This can be used to hide internet activity or be used to hide the process of exfiltrating data.
With this enabled organization will lose visibility into data such as query type, response and originating IP that are used to determine bad actors.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Edge\\BuiltInDnsClientEnabled' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)') OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Google\\Chrome\\DnsOverHttpsMode' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='secure') OR (TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\DNSOverHTTPS\\Enabled' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)')))
title: DNS-over-HTTPS Enabled by Registry

author: Matt Anderson (Huntress)
description:
Detects the use of powershell commands from headless ConHost window.
The "--headless" flag hides the windows from the user upon execution.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\conhost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='CONHOST.EXE') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%--headless%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%powershell%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Powershell Executed From Headless ConHost Process

author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects calls to "Add-Content" cmdlet in order to modify the content of the user profile and potentially adding suspicious commands for persistence
falsepositives: Legitimate administration and tuning scripts that aim to add functionality to a user PowerShell session
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Add-Content $profile%' ESCAPE '\' AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value "IEX %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value "Invoke-Expression%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value "Invoke-WebRequest%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value "Start-Process%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value ''IEX %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value ''Invoke-Expression%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value ''Invoke-WebRequest%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Value ''Start-Process%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential Persistence Via PowerShell User Profile Using Add-Content

author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
description:
Detects the execution of WMIC with the "format" flag to potentially load local XSL files.
Adversaries abuse this functionality to execute arbitrary files while potentially bypassing application whitelisting defenses.
Extensible Stylesheet Language (XSL) files are commonly used to describe the processing and rendering of data within XML files.
falsepositives: WMIC.exe FP depend on scripts and administrative methods used in the monitored environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wmic.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='wmic.exe' OR (Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=1B1A3F43BF37B5BFE60751F2EE2F326E%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=37777A96245A3C74EB217308F3546F4C%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=9D87C9D67CE724033C0B40CC4CA1B206%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=B12619881D79C3ACADF45E752A58554A%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=16A48C3CABF98A9DC1BF02C07FE1EA00%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-format:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/format:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%–format:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%—format:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%―format:%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((CommandLine LIKE '%Format:List%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:htable%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:hform%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:table%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:mof%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:value%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:rawxml%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:xml%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Format:csv%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%://%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\\\%' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: XSL Script Execution Via WMIC.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of winget to add new additional download sources
falsepositives: False positive are expected with legitimate sources
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\winget.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='winget.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%source %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%add %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Add New Download Source To Winget

author: Markus Neis, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, oscd.community
description: Detects Access to Domain Group Policies stored in SYSVOL
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%\\SYSVOL\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\policies\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious SYSVOL Domain Group Policy Access

author: frack113
description:
The DSInternals PowerShell Module exposes several internal features of Active Directory and Azure Active Directory.
These include FIDO2 and NGC key auditing, offline ntds.dit file manipulation, password auditing, DC recovery from IFM backups and password hash calculation.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-ADReplAccount%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-All %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Server %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious Get-ADReplAccount

author: frack113
description: Detects PowerShell scripts with potential registry reconnaissance capabilities. Adversaries may interact with the Windows registry to gather information about the system credentials, configuration, and installed software.
falsepositives: Due to the nature of the script block, the matching of the string could sometimes result in a false positive. Use this rule to hunt for potential malicious or suspicious scripts.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText REGEXP '(Get-Item|gci|Get-ChildItem).{1,64}-Path.{1,64}\\(currentcontrolset\\services|CurrentVersion\\Policies\\Explorer\\Run|CurrentVersion\\Run|CurrentVersion\\ShellServiceObjectDelayLoad|CurrentVersion\\Windows\winlogon)\\')
title: Potential Registry Reconnaissance Via PowerShell Script

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects attempts to delete Internet Information Services (IIS) log files via command line utilities, which is a common defense evasion technique used by attackers to cover their tracks.
Threat actors often abuse vulnerabilities in web applications hosted on IIS servers to gain initial access and later delete IIS logs to evade detection.
falsepositives: Deletion of IIS logs that are older than a certain retention period as part of regular maintenance activities.
Legitimate schedule tasks or scripts that clean up log files regularly.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell\_ise.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='cmd.exe' OR OriginalFileName='powershell.exe' OR OriginalFileName LIKE 'powershell\_ise.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%del %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%erase %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%rm %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%remove-item %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%rmdir %' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\inetpub\\logs\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: IIS WebServer Log Deletion via CommandLine Utilities

author: Victor Sergeev, oscd.community
description: Detects execution of "ftp.exe" script with the "-s" or "/s" flag and any child processes ran by "ftp.exe".
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\ftp.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\ftp.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='ftp.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-s:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/s:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%–s:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%—s:%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%―s:%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Potential Arbitrary Command Execution Via FTP.EXE

author: frack113
description: Powershell use PassThru option to start in background
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Start-Process %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%saps %' ESCAPE '\') AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-PassThru %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-FilePath %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Start-Process PassThru

author: Julia Fomina, oscd.community
description: Detects execution of attacker-controlled WsmPty.xsl or WsmTxt.xsl via winrm.vbs and copied cscript.exe (can be renamed)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%winrm%' ESCAPE '\' AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%format:pretty%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%format:"pretty"%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%format:"text"%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%format:text%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))))
title: AWL Bypass with Winrm.vbs and Malicious WsmPty.xsl/WsmTxt.xsl

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Scoubi (@ScoubiMtl)
description: Detects command line containing reference to the "::$index_allocation" stream, which can be used as a technique to prevent access to folders or files from tooling such as "explorer.exe" or "powershell.exe"
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND CommandLine LIKE '%::$index\_allocation%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Potential Hidden Directory Creation Via NTFS INDEX_ALLOCATION Stream - CLI

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects when an attacker adds a new "Debugger" value to the "AeDebug" key in order to achieve persistence which will get invoked when an application crashes
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the key to setup a debugger. Which is often the case on developers machines
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows NT\\CurrentVersion\\AeDebug\\Debugger%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '%.dll' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewValue LIKE '"C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\vsjitdebugger.exe" -p \%ld -e \%ld -j 0x\%p' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Add Debugger Entry To AeDebug For Persistence

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Endgame), oscd.community
description: Detects execition of commands and binaries from the context of The program compatibility assistant (Pcalua.exe). This can be used as a LOLBIN in order to bypass application whitelisting.
falsepositives: Legitimate use by a via a batch script or by an administrator.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pcalua.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% -a%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Use of Pcalua For Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects known WMI recon method to look for unquoted service paths, often used by pentest inside of powershell scripts attackers enum scripts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-WmiObject %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%gwmi %' ESCAPE '\') AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '% Win32\_Service %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Name%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%DisplayName%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%PathName%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%StartMode%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: WMIC Unquoted Services Path Lookup - PowerShell

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects potential installation or installation attempts of known malicious appx packages
falsepositives: Rare occasions where a malicious package uses the exact same name and version as a legitimate application.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Microsoft-Windows-AppXDeploymentServer/Operational' AND ((EventID=400 OR EventID=401) AND PackageFullName LIKE '%3669e262-ec02-4e9d-bcb4-3d008b4afac9%' ESCAPE '\')
title: Potential Malicious AppX Package Installation Attempts

author: Jose Luis Sanchez Martinez (@Joseliyo_Jstnk)
description: Detects the use of Jlaive to execute assemblies in a copied PowerShell
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentCommandLine LIKE '%.bat' ESCAPE '\') AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\xcopy.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%powershell.exe%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.bat.exe%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\xcopy.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%pwsh.exe%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.bat.exe%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\attrib.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%+s%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%+h%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.bat.exe%' ESCAPE '\')))))
title: HackTool - Jlaive In-Memory Assembly Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of wmic to start or stop a service
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((OriginalFileName='wmic.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\WMIC.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '% service %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% call %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%stopservice%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%startservice%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Service Started/Stopped Via Wmic.EXE

author: Ivan Dyachkov, oscd.community
description: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag. Attackers often abuse "diskshadow" to execute scripts that deleted the shadow copies on the systems. Investigate the content of the scripts and its location.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((OriginalFileName='diskshadow.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\diskshadow.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%–s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%—s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%―s %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Diskshadow Script Mode Execution

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Marco Pedrinazzi (@pedrinazziM) (InTheCyber)
description: Detects email forwarding or redirecting activity via ExchangePowerShell Cmdlet
falsepositives: Legitimate mail forwarding rules created by users or administrators to forward email to designated internal or external recipients for business or operational purposes.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%New-InboxRule%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Set-InboxRule%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Set-Mailbox%' ESCAPE '\') AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ForwardAsAttachmentTo%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ForwardingAddress%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ForwardingSmtpAddress%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ForwardTo%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%RedirectTo%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Mail Forwarding/Redirecting Activity Via ExchangePowerShell Cmdlet

author: Micah Babinski
description: Detects the use of rcedit to potentially alter executable PE metadata properties, which could conceal efforts to rename system utilities for defense evasion.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the tool by administrators or users to update metadata of a binary
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\rcedit-x64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\rcedit-x86.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR Description='Edit resources of exe' OR Product='rcedit') AND CommandLine LIKE '%--set-%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%OriginalFileName%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%CompanyName%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%FileDescription%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ProductName%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ProductVersion%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%LegalCopyright%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PUA - Potential PE Metadata Tamper Using Rcedit

author: frack113
description: Detect set Notification_Suppress to 1 to disable the Windows security center notification
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\UX Configuration\\Notification\_Suppress' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)'))
title: Activate Suppression of Windows Security Center Notifications

author: frack113
description:
Detects when an attacker tries to change User Account Control (UAC) elevation request destination via the "PromptOnSecureDesktop" value.
The "PromptOnSecureDesktop" setting specifically determines whether UAC prompts are displayed on the secure desktop. The secure desktop is a separate desktop environment that's isolated from other processes running on the system. It's designed to prevent malicious software from intercepting or tampering with UAC prompts.
When "PromptOnSecureDesktop" is set to 0, UAC prompts are displayed on the user's current desktop instead of the secure desktop. This reduces the level of security because it potentially exposes the prompts to manipulation by malicious software.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Policies\\System\\PromptOnSecureDesktop%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000000)'))
title: UAC Secure Desktop Prompt Disabled

author: @kostastsale
description:
Detects the execution of rundll32.exe with the oledb32.dll library to open a UDL file.
Threat actors can abuse this technique as a phishing vector to capture authentication credentials or other sensitive data.
falsepositives: UDL files serve as a convenient and flexible tool for managing and testing database connections in various development and administrative scenarios.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\rundll32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='RUNDLL32.EXE') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%oledb32.dll%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%,OpenDSLFile %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Users\\%\\Downloads\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%.udl' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potentially Suspicious Rundll32.EXE Execution of UDL File

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the creation of a dMSASvc account using the New-ADServiceAccount cmdlet in certain OUs.
The fact that the Cmdlet is used to create a dMSASvc account in a specific OU is highly suspicious.
It is a pattern trying to exploit the BadSuccessor privilege escalation vulnerability in Windows Server 2025.
On top of that, if the user that is creating the dMSASvc account is not a legitimate administrator or does not have the necessary permissions,
it is a strong signal of an attempted or successful abuse of the BaDSuccessor vulnerability for privilege escalation within the Windows Server 2025 Active Directory environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell\_ise.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='powershell.exe' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll' OR OriginalFileName LIKE 'powershell\_ise.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%New-ADServiceAccount%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-CreateDelegatedServiceAccount%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-path%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: New DMSA Service Account Created in Specific OUs

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of known powershell cmdlets such as "Clear-EventLog" to clear the Windows event logs
falsepositives: Rare need to clear logs before doing something. Sometimes used by installers or cleaner scripts. The script should be investigated to determine if it's legitimate
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Clear-EventLog %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Remove-EventLog %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Limit-EventLog %' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Clear-WinEvent %' ESCAPE '\') OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Eventing.Reader.EventLogSession%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ClearLog%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Diagnostics.EventLog%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Clear%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Eventlog Clear

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Hieu Tran
description: Detects potential DLL files being downloaded using the PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest or Invoke-RestMethod cmdlets.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-RestMethod %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-WebRequest %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%IRM %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%IWR %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%http%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%OutFile%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.dll%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential DLL File Download Via PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali
description: Detects execution of a renamed autohotkey.exe binary based on PE metadata fields
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((Product LIKE '%AutoHotkey%' ESCAPE '\' OR Description LIKE '%AutoHotkey%' ESCAPE '\' OR (OriginalFileName='AutoHotkey.exe' OR OriginalFileName='AutoHotkey.rc')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkey.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkey32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkey32\_UIA.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkey64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkey64\_UIA.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkeyA32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkeyA32\_UIA.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkeyU32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkeyU32\_UIA.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkeyU64.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkeyU64\_UIA.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AutoHotkey%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Renamed AutoHotkey.EXE Execution

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the execution "AccCheckConsole" a command-line tool for verifying the accessibility implementation of an application's UI.
One of the tests that this checker can run are called "verification routine", which tests for things like Consistency, Navigation, etc.
The tool allows a user to provide a DLL that can contain a custom "verification routine". An attacker can build such DLLs and pass it via the CLI, which would then be loaded in the context of the "AccCheckConsole" utility.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of the UI Accessibility Checker
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AccCheckConsole.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='AccCheckConsole.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -hwnd%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -process %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -window %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential DLL Injection Via AccCheckConsole

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by user inactivity.
Screensavers are programs that execute after a configurable time of user inactivity and consist of Portable Executable (PE) files with a .scr file extension
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%HKEY\_CURRENT\_USER\\Control Panel\\Desktop%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%HKCU\\Control Panel\\Desktop%' ESCAPE '\')) AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%/v ScreenSaveActive%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/t REG\_SZ%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/d 1%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/f%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%/v ScreenSaveTimeout%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/t REG\_SZ%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/d %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/f%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%/v ScreenSaverIsSecure%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/t REG\_SZ%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/d 0%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/f%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%/v SCRNSAVE.EXE%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/t REG\_SZ%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/d %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.scr%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/f%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Suspicious ScreenSave Change by Reg.exe

author: frack113
description: Detects usage of "ProtocolHandler" to download files. Downloaded files will be located in the cache folder (for example - %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\IE)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\protocolhandler.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='ProtocolHandler.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%ftp://%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%http://%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%https://%' ESCAPE '\')))
