title: Failed Logon From Public IP

author: frack113
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems by IP address, hostname, or other logical identifier on a network that may be used for Lateral Movement from the current system
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%for %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%foreach %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%nslookup%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%ping%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Scan Loop Network

author: frack113
description: Detects suspicious execution of 'Powercfg.exe' to change lock screen timeout
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powercfg.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='PowerCfg.exe') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%/setacvalueindex %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%SCHEME\_CURRENT%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%SUB\_VIDEO%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%VIDEOCONLOCK%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%-change %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-standby-timeout-%' ESCAPE '\'))))

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects potentially suspicious child process of applications launched from inside the WindowsApps directory. This could be a sign of a rogue ".appx" package installation/execution
falsepositives: Legitimate packages that make use of external binaries such as Windows Terminal
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\mshta.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell\_ise.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regsvr32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\rundll32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wscript.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%cmd /c%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Base64%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE(((ParentProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.WindowsTerminal%' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\WindowsTerminal.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\')) OR (ParentProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.SysinternalsSuite%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Potentially Suspicious Windows App Activity

author: frack113
description: Detects execution of PktMon, a tool that captures network packets.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pktmon.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='PktMon.exe'))
title: PktMon.EXE Execution

author: Ilyas Ochkov, Jonhnathan Ribeiro, Daniil Yugoslavskiy, oscd.community
description: Detects keywords that could indicate clearing PowerShell history
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND (((Payload LIKE '%Set-PSReadlineOption%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%–HistorySaveStyle%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%SaveNothing%' ESCAPE '\') OR (Payload LIKE '%Set-PSReadlineOption%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%-HistorySaveStyle%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%SaveNothing%' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((Payload LIKE '%del%' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%Remove-Item%' ESCAPE '\' OR Payload LIKE '%rm%' ESCAPE '\') AND Payload LIKE '%(Get-PSReadlineOption).HistorySavePath%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Clear PowerShell History - PowerShell Module

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of "Diskshadow.exe" in script mode using the "/s" flag where the script is located in a potentially suspicious location.
falsepositives: False positives may occur if you execute the script from one of the paths mentioned in the rule. Apply additional filters that fits your org needs.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((OriginalFileName='diskshadow.exe' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\diskshadow.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%–s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%—s %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%―s %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%:\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%:\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\AppData\\Roaming\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\ProgramData\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%\\Users\\Public\\%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Diskshadow Script Mode - Execution From Potential Suspicious Location

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of special strings/null bits in order to potentially bypass AMSI functionalities
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%if(0){{{0}}}'' -f $(0 -as [char]) +%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%#<NULL>%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potential AMSI Bypass Script Using NULL Bits

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to the AppInstaller (winget) policy. Specifically the activation of the local manifest installation, which allows a user to install new packages via custom manifests.
falsepositives: Administrators or developers might enable this for testing purposes or to install custom private packages
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\AppInstaller\\EnableLocalManifestFiles' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)'))
title: Enable Local Manifest Installation With Winget

author: X__Junior (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of "WerFault.exe" with the "-pr" commandline flag that is used to run files stored in the ReflectDebugger key which could be used to store the path to the malware in order to masquerade the execution flow
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\WerFault.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='WerFault.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '% -pr %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potential ReflectDebugger Content Execution Via WerFault.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects changes to the PowerShell execution policy in order to bypass signing requirements for script execution
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (((TargetObject LIKE '%\\ShellIds\\Microsoft.PowerShell\\ExecutionPolicy' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows\\PowerShell\\ExecutionPolicy' ESCAPE '\') AND (NewValue LIKE '%Bypass%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%Unrestricted%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Potential PowerShell Execution Policy Tampering

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the execution of the "cloudflared" binary from a non standard location.
falsepositives: Legitimate usage of Cloudflared portable versions
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cloudflared.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files (x86)\\cloudflared\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\cloudflared\\%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Cloudflared Portable Execution

author: frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the execution of "Extexport.exe".A utility that is part of the Internet Explorer browser and is used to export and import various settings and data, particularly when switching between Internet Explorer and other web browsers like Firefox. It allows users to transfer bookmarks, browsing history, and other preferences from Internet Explorer to Firefox or vice versa.
It can be abused as a tool to side load any DLL. If a folder is provided in the command line it'll load any DLL with one of the following names "mozcrt19.dll", "mozsqlite3.dll", or "sqlite.dll".
Arbitrary DLLs can also be loaded if a specific number of flags was provided.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Extexport.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='extexport.exe'))
title: Potential DLL Sideloading Activity Via ExtExport.EXE

author: frack113
description: Commandline to launch powershell with a base64 payload
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -e %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -en %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -enc %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -enco%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% -ec %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '% -Encoding %' ESCAPE '\' OR (ParentProcessName LIKE '%C:\\Packages\\Plugins\\Microsoft.GuestConfiguration.ConfigurationforWindows\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\gc\_worker.exe%' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Suspicious Execution of Powershell with Base64

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects PowerShell scripts that have capabilities to read files, loop through them and resolve DNS host entries.
falsepositives: The same functionality can be implemented by admin scripts, correlate with name and creator
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Get-content %' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%foreach%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%[System.Net.Dns]::GetHostEntry%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Out-File%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: PowerShell Script With File Hostname Resolving Capabilities

author: frack113
description: Executes arbitrary PowerShell code using SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='syncappvpublishingserver.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '%"n; %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: SyncAppvPublishingServer Execute Arbitrary PowerShell Code

author: frack113
description:
Adversaries may acquire credentials from web browsers by reading files specific to the target browser.
Web browsers commonly save credentials such as website usernames and passwords so that they do not need to be entered manually in the future.
Web browsers typically store the credentials in an encrypted format within a credential store.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Copy-Item%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%-Destination%' ESCAPE '\') AND (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%\\Opera Software\\Opera Stable\\Login Data%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Edge\\User Data\\Default%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data%' ESCAPE '\' OR ScriptBlockText LIKE '%\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data For Account%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Access to Browser Login Data

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects potential persistence activity via the registering of a new custom protocole handlers. While legitimate applications register protocole handlers often times during installation. And attacker can abuse this by setting a custom handler to be used as a persistence mechanism.
falsepositives: Many legitimate applications can register a new custom protocol handler. Additional filters needs to applied according to your environment.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE 'HKCR\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE 'URL:%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewValue LIKE 'URL:ms-%' ESCAPE '\' OR (NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Potential Persistence Via Custom Protocol Handler

author: Thomas Patzke, Romaissa Adjailia, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects launch of the PSEXESVC service, which means that this system was the target of a psexec remote execution
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\PSEXESVC.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='psexesvc.exe'))
title: PsExec Service Execution

author: frack113
description: Detect use of scrobj.dll as this DLL looks for the ScriptletURL key to get the location of the script to execute
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%InprocServer32\\(Default)' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE 'C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\scrobj.dll' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Potential Persistence Via Scrobj.dll COM Hijacking

author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, OSCD Community
description: Detects SyncAppvPublishingServer process execution which usually utilized by adversaries to bypass PowerShell execution restrictions.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND ContextInfo LIKE '%SyncAppvPublishingServer.exe%' ESCAPE '\')
title: SyncAppvPublishingServer Bypass Powershell Restriction - PS Module

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), X__Junior (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the creation of a schedule task that runs weekly and execute the "shutdown /l /f" command.
This behavior was observed being used by KamiKakaBot samples in order to achieve persistence on a system.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '% /create %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%shutdown /l /f%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%WEEKLY%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((User LIKE '%AUTHORI%' ESCAPE '\' OR User LIKE '%AUTORI%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Potential KamiKakaBot Activity - Shutdown Schedule Task Creation

author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC
description:
This detection uses Windows security events to detect suspicious access attempts to the registry key of Azure AD Health monitoring agent.
This detection requires an access control entry (ACE) on the system access control list (SACL) of the following securable object HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft Online\Reporting\MonitoringAgent.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (((EventID=4656 OR EventID=4663) AND ObjectType='Key' AND ObjectName LIKE '\\REGISTRY\\MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Microsoft Online\\Reporting\\MonitoringAgent' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((ProcessName LIKE '%Microsoft.Identity.Health.Adfs.DiagnosticsAgent.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%Microsoft.Identity.Health.Adfs.InsightsService.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%Microsoft.Identity.Health.Adfs.MonitoringAgent.Startup.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%Microsoft.Identity.Health.Adfs.PshSurrogate.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessName LIKE '%Microsoft.Identity.Health.Common.Clients.ResourceMonitor.exe%' ESCAPE '\'), 0)))
title: Azure AD Health Monitoring Agent Registry Keys Access

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects creation of a scheduled task with a GUID like name
falsepositives: Legitimate software naming their tasks as GUIDs
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/Create %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/TN "{%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/TN ''{%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/TN {%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%}"%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%}''%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%} %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Name As GUID

author: oscd.community, @redcanary, Zach Stanford @svch0st
description:
Detects execution of "certmgr" with the "add" flag in order to install a new certificate on the system.
Adversaries may install a root certificate on a compromised system to avoid warnings when connecting to adversary controlled web servers.
falsepositives: Help Desk or IT may need to manually add a corporate Root CA on occasion. Need to test if GPO push doesn't trigger FP
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\CertMgr.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='CERTMGT.EXE') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/add%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%root%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: New Root Certificate Installed Via CertMgr.EXE

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Tim Shelton (HAWK.IO), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects a suspicious copy operation that tries to copy a program from system (System32, SysWOW64, WinSxS) directories to another on disk.
Often used to move LOLBINs such as 'certutil' or 'desktopimgdownldr' to a different location with a different name in order to bypass detections based on locations.
falsepositives: Depend on scripts and administrative tools used in the monitored environment (For example an admin scripts like https://www.itexperience.net/sccm-batch-files-and-32-bits-processes-on-64-bits-os/)
When cmd.exe and xcopy.exe are called directly
When the command contains the keywords but not in the correct order
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%copy %' ESCAPE '\') OR ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%copy-item%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% copy %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cpi %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% cp %' ESCAPE '\')) OR ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\robocopy.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\xcopy.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='robocopy.exe' OR OriginalFileName='XCOPY.EXE'))) AND CommandLine REGEXP '(?i)\s[''"]?C:\\Windows\\(?:System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%/c copy%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\avira\_system\_speedup.exe%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\Program Files\\Avira\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Avira\\%' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))
title: Suspicious Copy From or To System Directory

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects a specific command line of "regsvr32" where the "calc" keyword is used in conjunction with the "/s" flag. This behavior is often seen used by Qakbot
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regsvr32.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —s%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―s%' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '% calc' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Qakbot Regsvr32 Calc Pattern

author: Christian Burkard (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the pattern of UAC Bypass using Windows Media Player osksupport.dll (UACMe 32)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Media Player\\osk.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR (NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentCommandLine LIKE '"C:\\Windows\\system32\\mmc.exe" "C:\\Windows\\system32\\eventvwr.msc" /s' ESCAPE '\')) AND (IntegrityLevel='High' OR IntegrityLevel='System' OR IntegrityLevel='S-1-16-16384' OR IntegrityLevel='S-1-16-12288')))
title: UAC Bypass Using Windows Media Player - Process

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects suspicious ways to download files from Microsoft domains that are used to store attachments in Emails or OneNote documents
falsepositives: Scripts or tools that download attachments from these domains (OneNote, Outlook 365)
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\curl.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wget.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%Invoke-WebRequest%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%iwr %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%curl %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%wget %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Start-BitsTransfer%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.DownloadFile(%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.DownloadString(%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%https://attachment.outlook.live.net/owa/%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%https://onenoteonlinesync.onenote.com/onenoteonlinesync/%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious Download from Office Domain

author: Sander Wiebing
description: Detects usage of the netsh command to open and allow connections to port 3389 (RDP). As seen used by Sarwent Malware
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\netsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='netsh.exe') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%firewall %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%add %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%tcp %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%3389%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%portopening%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%allow%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: RDP Connection Allowed Via Netsh.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the execution of PowerShell with a specific flag sequence that is used by the Wmiexec script
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND CommandLine LIKE '%-NoP -NoL -sta -NonI -W Hidden -Exec Bypass -Enc%' ESCAPE '\')
title: HackTool - Wmiexec Default Powershell Command

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects suspicious Hangul Word Processor (Hanword) sub processes that could indicate an exploitation
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\Hwp.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\gbb.exe' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Suspicious HWP Sub Processes

author: @Kostastsale
description:
Detects changes to the registry value "PythonFunctionWarnings" that would prevent any warnings or alerts from showing when Python functions are about to be executed.
Threat actors could run malicious code through the new Microsoft Excel feature that allows Python to run within the spreadsheet.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Office\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Excel\\Security%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%PythonFunctionWarnings%' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '% 0%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Python Function Execution Security Warning Disabled In Excel

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects a specific command line arguments sequence seen used by SNAKE malware during its installation as described by CISA in their report
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND CommandLine REGEXP '\s[a-fA-F0-9]{64}\s[a-fA-F0-9]{16}')
title: Potential SNAKE Malware Installation CLI Arguments Indicator

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, Sander Wiebing, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects suspicious new RUN key element pointing to an executable in a suspicious folder
falsepositives: Software using weird folders for updates

'%\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Software\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%:\\Windows\\Temp%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%:\\Temp%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\AppData\\Roaming%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%:\\$Recycle.bin%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%:\\Users\\Default%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%:\\Users\\public%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\%temp\%%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\%tmp\%%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\%Public\%%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\%AppData\%%' ESCAPE '\') OR (NewValue LIKE '%:\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewValue LIKE '%\\Favorites%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\Favourites%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\Contacts%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\Music%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\Pictures%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%\\Documents%' ESCAPE 'C:\\Windows\\SoftwareDistribution\\Download\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewValue LIKE '%rundll32.exe %' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '%C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\advpack.dll,DelNodeRunDLL32%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NewValue LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewValue LIKE '%C:\\Windows\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\')), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((NewProcessName LIKE '%C:\\Program Files\\Spotify\\Spotify.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Spotify\\Spotify.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Roaming\\Spotify\\Spotify.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND TargetObject LIKE '%SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\Spotify' ESCAPE '\' AND NewValue LIKE '%Spotify.exe --autostart --minimized' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), oscd.community, Jonhnathan Ribeiro
description: Detects Formbook like process executions that inject code into a set of files in the System32 folder, which executes a special command command line to delete the dropper from the AppData Temp folder. We avoid false positives by excluding all parent process with command line parameters.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((ParentCommandLine LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentCommandLine LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND ParentCommandLine LIKE '%.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%/c%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%del%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%/c%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%del%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Desktop\\%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%/C%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%type nul >%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%C:\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Desktop\\%' ESCAPE '\')) AND CommandLine LIKE '%.exe' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Formbook Process Creation

author: Aleksey Potapov, oscd.community
description: Detects SILENTTRINITY stager use via PE metadata
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND Description LIKE '%st2stager%' ESCAPE '\')
title: HackTool - SILENTTRINITY Stager Execution

author: Michael Haag
description: Detects a suspicious process spawning from an "mshta.exe" process, which could be indicative of a malicious HTA script execution
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\mshta.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\bash.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regsvr32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\bitsadmin.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe' OR OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll' OR OriginalFileName='wscript.exe' OR OriginalFileName='cscript.exe' OR OriginalFileName='Bash.exe' OR OriginalFileName='reg.exe' OR OriginalFileName='REGSVR32.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='bitsadmin.exe'))))
title: Suspicious MSHTA Child Process

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community
description:
Detects usage of WinAPI functions in PowerShell scripts.
It may indicate attempts to perform actions such as process injection, token stealing, or other malicious activities that leverage Windows API calls.
These techniques are commonly used to evade traditional file-based detections by loading and executing code directly in memory.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ((ScriptBlockText LIKE '%VirtualAlloc%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%OpenProcess%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%WriteProcessMemory%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%CreateRemoteThread%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%OpenProcessToken%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%LookupPrivilegeValue%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%AdjustTokenPrivileges%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%OpenProcessToken%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%DuplicateTokenEx%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%CloseHandle%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%WriteProcessMemory%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%VirtualAlloc%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%ReadProcessMemory%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%VirtualFree%' ESCAPE '\') OR (ScriptBlockText LIKE '%VirtualAlloc%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%GetDelegateForFunctionPointer%' ESCAPE '\' AND ScriptBlockText LIKE '%Marshal.Copy%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential WinAPI Calls Via PowerShell Scripts

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Microsoft (idea)
description: Detects a suspicious IIS module registration as described in Microsoft threat report on IIS backdoors
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\w3wp.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%appcmd.exe add module%' ESCAPE '\' OR (CommandLine LIKE '% system.enterpriseservices.internal.publish%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%gacutil%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% /I%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Suspicious IIS Module Registration

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of the copy builtin cmd command to copy files with the ".dmp"/".dump" extension from a remote share
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='Cmd.Exe') AND ((CommandLine LIKE '%copy %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '% \\\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%.dmp%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.dump%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.hdmp%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: Copy .DMP/.DUMP Files From Remote Share Via Cmd.EXE

author: Luca Di Bartolomeo (CrimpSec)
description: Detects the execution of SharpMove, a .NET utility performing multiple tasks such as "Task Creation", "SCM" query, VBScript execution using WMI via its PE metadata and command line options.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\SharpMove.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='SharpMove.exe') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%computername=%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%action=create%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=dcom%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=executevbs%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=hijackdcom%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=modschtask%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=modsvc%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=query%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=scm%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=startservice%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%action=taskscheduler%' ESCAPE '\'))))
title: HackTool - SharpMove Tool Execution

author: Thomas Patzke
description: Detects various execution patterns of the CrackMapExec pentesting framework
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%cmd.exe /Q /c % 1> \\\\%\\%\\% 2>&1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cmd.exe /C % > \\\\%\\%\\% 2>&1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%cmd.exe /C % > %\\Temp\\% 2>&1%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%powershell.exe -exec bypass -noni -nop -w 1 -C "%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%powershell.exe -noni -nop -w 1 -enc %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: HackTool - CrackMapExec Execution Patterns

author: Karneades, Swisscom CSIRT
description: Detects a Windows command line executable started from MMC
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\mmc.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\bash.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regsvr32.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\BITSADMIN%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: MMC Spawning Windows Shell

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of "reg.exe" commands with the "delete" flag on services registry key. Often used by attacker to remove AV software services
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%reg.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='reg.exe') AND CommandLine LIKE '% delete %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\services\\%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Service Registry Key Deleted Via Reg.EXE

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description:
An adversary may use legitimate desktop support and remote access software, such as Team Viewer, Go2Assist, LogMein, AmmyyAdmin, etc, to establish an interactive command and control channel to target systems within networks.
These services are commonly used as legitimate technical support software, and may be allowed by application control within a target environment.
Remote access tools like VNC, Ammyy, and Teamviewer are used frequently when compared with other legitimate software commonly used by adversaries. (Citation: Symantec Living off the Land)
falsepositives: Legitimate use of AnyDesk from a non-standard folder
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AnyDesk.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AnyDeskMSI.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR Description='AnyDesk' OR Product='AnyDesk' OR Company='AnyDesk Software GmbH') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%Program Files (x86)\\AnyDesk%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%Program Files\\AnyDesk%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Remote Access Tool - Anydesk Execution From Suspicious Folder

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of the Quarks PwDump tool via commandline arguments
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\QuarksPwDump.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR (CommandLine=' -dhl' OR CommandLine=' --dump-hash-local' OR CommandLine=' -dhdc' OR CommandLine=' --dump-hash-domain-cached' OR CommandLine=' --dump-bitlocker' OR CommandLine=' -dhd ' OR CommandLine=' --dump-hash-domain ' OR CommandLine='--ntds-file')))
title: HackTool - Quarks PwDump Execution

author: Omkar Gudhate
description: Detects changes to 'HKCU\Software\Classes\Folder\shell\open\command\DelegateExecute'
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND TargetObject LIKE '%\\Software\\Classes\\Folder\\shell\\open\\command\\DelegateExecute%' ESCAPE '\')
title: COM Hijack via Sdclt

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of the built-in script located in "C:\Windows\System32\gatherNetworkInfo.vbs". Which can be used to gather information about the target machine
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%gatherNetworkInfo.vbs%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wscript.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Suspicious Reconnaissance Activity Via GatherNetworkInfo.VBS

author: Nikita Nazarov, oscd.community
description: Detects Obfuscated Powershell via use MSHTA in Scripts
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4103 AND (Payload LIKE '%set%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%&&%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%mshta%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%vbscript:createobject%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%.run%' ESCAPE '\' AND Payload LIKE '%(window.close)%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Invoke-Obfuscation Via Use MSHTA - PowerShell Module

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the execution of specific processes and command line combination.
These were seen being created by Forest Blizzard as described by MSFT.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((Hashes LIKE '%SHA256=6b311c0a977d21e772ac4e99762234da852bbf84293386fbe78622a96c0b052f%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%SHA256=c60ead92cd376b689d1b4450f2578b36ea0bf64f3963cfa5546279fa4424c2a5%' ESCAPE '\') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Create%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/RU%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%SYSTEM%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WinSrv%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%servtask.bat%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%execute.bat%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%doit.bat%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\schtasks.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Delete%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%/F %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%\\Microsoft\\Windows\\WinSrv%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%Get-ChildItem%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%.save%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%Compress-Archive -DestinationPath C:\\ProgramData\\%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Forest Blizzard APT - Process Creation Activity

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects attempts to remove Windows Defender configurations using the 'MpPreference' cmdlet
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Remove-MpPreference%' ESCAPE '\' AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-ControlledFolderAccessProtectedFolders %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-AttackSurfaceReductionRules\_Ids %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-AttackSurfaceReductionRules\_Actions %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-CheckForSignaturesBeforeRunningScan %' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Tamper Windows Defender Remove-MpPreference

author: jmallette, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects usage of cmdkey to look for cached credentials on the system
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmdkey.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='cmdkey.exe') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% -l%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% /l%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% –l%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% —l%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% ―l%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Potential Reconnaissance For Cached Credentials Via Cmdkey.EXE

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects when an attacker tries to backdoor the MSSQL server by adding a backdoor account to the sysadmin fixed server role
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Application' AND (Provider_Name LIKE '%MSSQL%' ESCAPE '\' AND EventID=33205 AND (Data LIKE '%object\_name:sysadmin%' ESCAPE '\' AND Data LIKE '%statement:alter server role [sysadmin] add member %' ESCAPE '\'))
title: MSSQL Add Account To Sysadmin Role

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects modification addition to the 'TypedPaths' key in the user or admin registry from a non standard application. Which might indicate persistence attempt
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND (TargetObject LIKE '%\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\TypedPaths\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Potential Persistence Via TypedPaths

author: xknow @xknow_infosec, Tim Shelton
description: Detects potential path traversal attempt via cmd.exe. Could indicate possible command/argument confusion/hijacking
falsepositives: Java tools are known to produce false-positive when loading libraries
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='cmd.exe') AND ((ParentCommandLine LIKE '%/c%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentCommandLine LIKE '%/k%' ESCAPE '\' OR ParentCommandLine LIKE '%/r%' ESCAPE '\') OR (CommandLine LIKE '%/c%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/k%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/r%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (ParentCommandLine='/../../' OR CommandLine LIKE '%/../../%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((CommandLine LIKE '%\\Tasktop\\keycloak\\bin\\/../../jre\\bin\\java%' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Potential CommandLine Path Traversal Via Cmd.EXE

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), frack113
description: Detects the execution of REGSVR32.exe with DLL files masquerading as other files
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regsvr32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='REGSVR32.EXE') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%.bin' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.bmp' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.cr2' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.dat' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.eps' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.gif' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.ico' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.jpeg' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.jpg' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.log' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.nef' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.orf' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.png' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.raw' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.rtf' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.sr2' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.temp' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.tif' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.tiff' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.tmp' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.txt' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Regsvr32 DLL Execution With Suspicious File Extension

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Huntress DE&TH Team (idea)
description: Detects suspicious child processes of "pc-app.exe". Which could indicate potential exploitation of PaperCut
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\pc-app.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\bash.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\calc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\certutil.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cmd.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\csc.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\cscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\dllhost.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\mshta.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msiexec.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\regsvr32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\rundll32.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\scriptrunner.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wmic.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wscript.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\wsl.exe' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PaperCut MF/NG Potential Exploitation

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects PowerShell scripts to set the ACL to a file in the Windows folder
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE' OR OriginalFileName='pwsh.dll') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%Set-Acl %' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%-AclObject %' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%-Path "C:\\Windows%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-Path ''C:\\Windows%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-Path \%windir\%%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%-Path $env:windir%' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%FullControl%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%Allow%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: PowerShell Set-Acl On Windows Folder

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects suspicious ways to run Invoke-Execution using IEX alias
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\pwsh.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '% | iex;%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | iex %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | iex}%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | IEX ;%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | IEX -Error%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | IEX (new%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%);IEX %' ESCAPE '\')) AND (CommandLine LIKE '%::FromBase64String%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%.GetString([System.Convert]::%' ESCAPE '\')) OR (CommandLine LIKE '%)|iex;$%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%);iex($%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%);iex $%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | IEX | %' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '% | iex\\"%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Suspicious PowerShell IEX Execution Patterns

author: Janantha Marasinghe (https://github.com/blueteam0ps)
description:
Threat actors can use auditpol binary to change audit policy configuration to impair detection capability.
This can be carried out by selectively disabling/removing certain audit policies as well as restoring a custom policy owned by the threat actor.
falsepositives: Administrator or administrator scripts might leverage the flags mentioned in the detection section. Either way, it should always be monitored
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\auditpol.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName='AUDITPOL.EXE') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%disable%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%clear%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%remove%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%restore%' ESCAPE '\')))
title: Audit Policy Tampering Via Auditpol

author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of the Notepad++ updater in a suspicious directory, which is often used in DLL side-loading attacks
falsepositives: Execution of tools named GUP.exe and located in folders different than Notepad++\updater
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\GUP.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE(((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Program Files\\Notepad++\\updater\\GUP.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Program Files (x86)\\Notepad++\\updater\\GUP.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Users\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Notepad++\\updater\\GUP.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Roaming\\Notepad++\\updater\\GUP.exe' ESCAPE '\'))), 0))))
title: Suspicious GUP Usage

author: @kostastsale
description: Detects execution of ChromeLoader malware via a registered scheduled task
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\powershell.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND ParentCommandLine LIKE '%-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Hidden -E JAB%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%--load-extension="%\\Appdata\\local\\chrome"%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\chrome.exe' ESCAPE '\'))
title: ChromeLoader Malware Execution

author: Tom Ueltschi (@c_APT_ure), Tim Shelton
description: Detects uncommon "userinit.exe" child processes, which could be a sign of uncommon shells or login scripts used for persistence.
falsepositives: Legitimate logon scripts or custom shells may trigger false positives. Apply additional filters accordingly.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (ParentProcessName LIKE '%\\userinit.exe' ESCAPE '\' AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\WINDOWS\\explorer.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0)) AND (NOT COALESCE(((CommandLine LIKE '%netlogon.bat%' ESCAPE '\' OR CommandLine LIKE '%UsrLogon.cmd%' ESCAPE '\') OR CommandLine='PowerShell.exe' OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\System32\\proquota.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\proquota.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR (NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\cmstart.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\icast.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files (x86)\\Citrix\\System32\\icast.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\cmstart.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\Citrix\\HDX\\bin\\icast.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%:\\Program Files\\Citrix\\System32\\icast.exe' ESCAPE '\') OR NewProcessName IS NULL), 0))))
title: Uncommon Userinit Child Process

author: Jonathan Cheong, oscd.community
description: Detects Obfuscated use of Environment Variables to execute PowerShell
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' OR Channel='PowerShellCore/Operational') AND (EventID=4104 AND ScriptBlockText REGEXP 'cmd.{0,5}(?:/c|/r)(?:\s|)"set\s[a-zA-Z]{3,6}.*(?:\{\d\}){1,}\\"\s+?-f(?:.*\)){1,}.*"')
title: Invoke-Obfuscation VAR+ Launcher - PowerShell

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the execution of a renamed "client32.exe" (NetSupport RAT) via Imphash, Product and OriginalFileName strings
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND ((Product LIKE '%NetSupport Remote Control%' ESCAPE '\' OR OriginalFileName LIKE '%client32.exe%' ESCAPE '\' OR Hashes LIKE '%IMPHASH=A9D50692E95B79723F3E76FCF70D023E%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\client32.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))

author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects the execution of a renamed office binary

author: Bhabesh Raj
description: Detects Code Integrity (CI) engine blocking Microsoft Defender's processes (MpCmdRun and NisSrv) from loading unsigned DLLs which may be an attempt to sideload arbitrary DLL
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE (Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Security-Mitigations/Kernel Mode' OR Channel='Microsoft-Windows-Security-Mitigations/User Mode') AND ((EventID=11 OR EventID=12) AND (ProcessPath LIKE '%\\MpCmdRun.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR ProcessPath LIKE '%\\NisSrv.exe' ESCAPE '\'))

author: Ensar Şamil, @sblmsrsn, @oscd_initiative

author: Sreeman, Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description: Detects execution of chromium based browser in headless mode using the "dump-dom" command line to download files
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\brave.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\chrome.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msedge.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\opera.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\vivaldi.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND (CommandLine LIKE '%--headless%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%dump-dom%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%http%' ESCAPE '\')) AND (NOT COALESCE((((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\EdgeCore\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Microsoft\\EdgeWebView\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\EdgeCore\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft\\EdgeWebView\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msedge.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msedgewebview2.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\MicrosoftEdge.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%--headless --disable-gpu --disable-extensions --disable-plugins --mute-audio --no-first-run --incognito --aggressive-cache-discard --dump-dom%' ESCAPE '\') OR ((NewProcessName LIKE '%\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\Windows\\SystemApps\\Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge%' ESCAPE '\') AND (NewProcessName LIKE '%\\msedge.exe' ESCAPE '\' OR NewProcessName LIKE '%\\MicrosoftEdge.exe' ESCAPE '\') AND CommandLine LIKE '%--headless --disable-gpu --disable-extensions --disable-plugins --mute-audio --no-first-run --incognito --aggressive-cache-discard --dump-dom%' ESCAPE '\')), 0))))

author: AlertIQ, Ján Trenčanský, frack113, Nasreddine Bencherchali, Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel
description: Detects when attackers or tools disable Windows Defender functionalities via the Windows registry
falsepositives: Administrator actions via the Windows Defender interface
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND ((EventID=4657 AND OperationType='Existing registry value modified') AND ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender Security Center\\%' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\SOFTWARE\\Policies\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\%' ESCAPE '\') AND (((TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableAntiSpyware' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableAntiVirus' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableBehaviorMonitoring' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableBlockAtFirstSeen' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableEnhancedNotifications' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableIntrusionPreventionSystem' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableIOAVProtection' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableOnAccessProtection' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableRealtimeMonitoring' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableScanOnRealtimeEnable' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisableScriptScanning' ESCAPE '\') AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000001)') OR ((TargetObject LIKE '%\\DisallowExploitProtectionOverride' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Features\\TamperProtection' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\MpEngine\\MpEnablePus' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\PUAProtection' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Signature Update\\ForceUpdateFromMU' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\SpyNet\\SpynetReporting' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\SpyNet\\SubmitSamplesConsent' ESCAPE '\' OR TargetObject LIKE '%\\Windows Defender Exploit Guard\\Controlled Folder Access\\EnableControlledFolderAccess' ESCAPE '\') AND NewValue='DWORD (0x00000000)')) AND (NOT COALESCE((NewProcessName LIKE 'C:\\Program Files\\Symantec\\Symantec Endpoint Protection\\%' ESCAPE '\' AND NewProcessName LIKE '%\\sepWscSvc64.exe' ESCAPE '\'), 0))))
title: Disable Windows Defender Functionalities Via Registry Keys

author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects the presence of "UWhRC....AAYBAAAA" pattern in command line.
The pattern "1UWhRCAAAAA..BAAAA" is a base64-encoded signature that corresponds to a marshaled CREDENTIAL_TARGET_INFORMATION structure.
Attackers can use this technique to coerce authentication from victim systems to attacker-controlled hosts.
It is one of the strong indicators of a Kerberos coercion attack, where adversaries manipulate DNS records
to spoof Service Principal Names (SPNs) and redirect authentication requests like in CVE-2025-33073.
If you see this pattern in the command line, it is likely an attempt to add spoofed Service Principal Names (SPNs) to DNS records,
or checking for the presence of such records through the `nslookup` command.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4688 AND (CommandLine LIKE '%UWhRCA%' ESCAPE '\' AND CommandLine LIKE '%BAAAA%' ESCAPE '\'))
title: Attempts of Kerberos Coercion Via DNS SPN Spoofing

author: Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research)
description: Rule to detect the Hybrid Connection Manager service installation.
falsepositives: Legitimate use of Hybrid Connection Manager via Azure function apps.
rule: SELECT * FROM logs WHERE Channel='Security' AND (EventID=4697 AND ServiceName='HybridConnectionManager' AND ServiceFileName LIKE '%HybridConnectionManager%' ESCAPE '\')
